_comment: GHIDRA FINDINGS QUEUE -- Ghidra-side corrections noticed by sessions that cannot write to the DB.
WHY THIS EXISTS. An unattended batch session (tools/ai_loop.py) reads exported .asm/.c and has no
ReVA connection, so it cannot fix a wrong prototype, a swapped parameter name or a misleading
plate the moment it finds one. Those findings are exactly the ones worth keeping -- the
layer-5 `resource_site_meets_threshold` correction of 2026-08-01 (Ghidra said `building_idx`,
the caller said `resource_kind`, and BOTH were wrong) came out of precisely this situation. The
queue is how a finding survives the session that noticed it.
This is the same discipline CLAUDE.md already sets for fan-outs: read-only workers SURFACE
evidence, the central (human-supervised, ReVA-live) session applies. It is NOT a place to record
open RE questions -- those go to tasks/*.md. Only concrete, checkable DB corrections belong here.
BLOCKING vs INCIDENTAL, and the distinction matters:
incidental -- the wrong metadata is on some OTHER function. Queue it and carry on.
blocking   -- the wrong metadata is on the function being translated RIGHT NOW. Queue it with
`blocking: true` AND end the session BLOCKED. A translation written against a
prototype known to be wrong is a wrong translation, and the module rules forbid
working around it with byte offsets.
DRAINING IT is a prep session's job (ReVA live, per the ai-migration-session skill's session
types): verify each finding against the disassembly, apply names/plates/tags via
tools/apply_annotations.py and prototypes via tools/commit_prototypes.py, save + check in, commit,
then set each entry's `status` with a `resolution` saying what you changed relative to the finding
and why. Entries are KEPT after resolution -- the trail of what a batch session caught is worth
having.
FOUR STATUS VALUES (`deferred` added 2026-08-03):
open      -- UNSETTLED. Nobody has re-derived it; a reader of that metadata may be reading a lie.
applied   -- done.
rejected  -- re-derived, and the finding was wrong. Say what the evidence actually shows.
deferred  -- SETTLED AND SCHEDULED. Requires ALL THREE of: the mechanism re-derived, the
plate/field comment already corrected so no reader can be misled, and only a
mechanical apply remaining -- which the `resolution` must name step by step.
WHY `deferred` EXISTS. The queue used to have one holding value, so 'I proved what this is, fixed
the plate, and the rename still needs spelling through four files' and 'nobody has checked this'
were the same word. ai_loop.py halts on the pile depth, and the stated reason for that halt is that
later translations rest on metadata already known to be wrong -- which is false of the first kind
and true of the second. The 2026-08-02-2349 drain applied 2, raised 1, re-deferred 4, and left the
queue at exactly the threshold it started at; the loop stopped with nothing actually unsettled.
Use `deferred` honestly: if the mechanism is still in doubt it is `open`, whatever the plate says.
tools/ai_loop.py counts `open` and `deferred` separately, records both in its ledger, and halts the
loop on `open` alone (MAX_OPEN_FINDINGS). Deferrals have a looser cap that routes a prep session
rather than stopping, purely so the backlog cannot grow without bound.

findings.current: Plate says the function 'releases a pending-construction-queue slot ... matching order_id' and closes with 'Distinct sentinel type bytes gate different queue-slot categories (-0x7d seen for mode 0; others not fully distinguished).' Two problems. (1) It calls the second parameter order_id; the COMMITTED PROTOTYPE calls it building_index and the prototype is the correct one, so the plate contradicts the signature printed directly above it in every decompile. (2) The sentinel is written as the signed byte -0x7d and described as not fully distinguished, when it is 0x83 and its sibling 0x84, both of which the ai_bldg_queue_entry.status field comment already documents by name (0x80 = finished/committed OR'd with kind nibble 3 = repair / 4 = upgrade).
findings.proposed: Rewrite the plate as: matches on building_index (NOT an order id) and dispatches on `mode`, UNSIGNED, over exactly {0,1,2} -- anything else, including a negative, returns. mode 0 = the job COMPLETED: on a committed REPAIR entry (status == 0x83) decrement tick_or_unit_id if non-zero, then subtract resource_reserved[1..4] (ZERO-extended) from resource_spent[1..4]; a committed UPGRADE entry (0x84) matching FIRST ends the scan with no effect at all -- an early-out, not a fall-through. mode 1 = cancel a repair: status |= 0x40 on the matching 0x83 entry. mode 2 = the same on the matching 0x84 entry. The scan is bounded by ai_bldg_queue_count and returns on the FIRST match. Whole-byte status compare, not the kind nibble. Also worth a `conf:high` tag in place of the current `conf:med`, and the `todo:globals` tag can be dropped: the function's only globals are player_data fields, all now named and typed.
findings.evidence: Disassembly tmp/decomp_aiprep/llm_strat_ai_queue_release_order_004dbf36.asm. Parameter identity: ESI (param 2) is compared at 0x004dbf9a / 0x004dc029 / 0x004dc06d / 0x004dc0b3 against [EAX+0xe935fe], which is ai_bldg_queue[i].building_index (player_data base 0xe6dec0 + 0x25730 + 0xe; the base follows from ai_enabled @0xe6ded8 - 0x18 and reproduces all thirteen absolutes in the listing). Mode dispatch: CMP EBX,1 / JC at 0x004dbf66-69 (mode 0), JBE at 0x004dbf6b (mode 1), CMP EBX,2 / JZ at 0x004dbf71 (mode 2), otherwise the RET at 0x004dbf7c -- all UNSIGNED. Sentinels: CMP byte [..],0x83 at 0x004dbf91 and 0x004dc064; CMP byte [..],0x84 at 0x004dc020 and 0x004dc0aa. The mode-0 upgrade early-out is the JZ 0x004dc0da at 0x004dc02f, which targets the bare POP/POP/RET epilogue. The stamp is OR byte [..],0x40 at 0x004dc075. SECOND DERIVATION for the write set: the state matrix (tmp/state_matrix.json) attributes this function exactly one region, player_data, with 6 read-modify-writes -- the four resource_spent SUBs at 0x004dbfd2 / dfe0 / dfee / dffc, the DEC at 0x004dbfab and the OR at 0x004dc075, and nothing else.
findings.why_not_blocking: The COMMITTED PROTOTYPE is correct -- (int player, int building_index, int mode) matches the disassembly's EAX/EDX/EBX storage and the field the second parameter is compared against -- and the translation was written against the .asm, not the plate. Only the plate PROSE is stale, so no translation rests on it.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v190) with TWO CORRECTIONS -- and the corrections are the point, because they are what the conductor's independent re-check is for. Every MECHANICAL claim verified against a freshly exported listing: the prototype, the unsigned {0,1,2} dispatch, both 0x83/0x84 sentinel pairs, the 0x40 stamp at 0x004dc075, the mode-0 early-out JZ at 0x004dc02f into the bare epilogue, and the 0x12 entry stride (IMUL EBX,EDX,0x12 at 0x004dbf8c). Two claims did NOT survive. (1) THE SEMANTIC WAS BACKWARDS. The finding labelled mode 0 'the job COMPLETED'; the call sites say the opposite. mode 0 is called by llm_strat_bldg_state_charge_gate on the branch where llm_strat_bldg_pay_cycle_inputs FAILED and the state goes back to CHARGE_STEP with no completion dispatch -- it backs a stalled tick out and releases its reservation. The COMPLETION paths are modes 1 and 2, both immediately followed by llm_strat_bldg_completion_dispatch, and both stamping 0x40, which the status field comment already defines as 'entry removed'. Writing the finding's label into the DB would have put a confident wrong semantic on a function whose branch importance a future reviewer judges from exactly that sentence. The finding's evidence justified the mechanics and never the label -- it was the one assertion with no citation. (2) THE TAG PROPOSAL REFERRED TO TAGS THAT DO NOT EXIST: it asked to replace conf:med and drop todo:globals, and the function carries NO tags at all in either ReVA or the manifest. Applied conf:high alone. Also noted, not applied: the finding said 'its two sim call sites'; there are five references from three functions (charge_gate x3, bldg_state_upgrading, order_queue_dispatch).

findings.current: UNNAMED. mh_game_player_data carries +0x28488..+0x284c7 as `uint8_t _pad_0x28488[64]`, i.e. undefined padding. The field comment on ai_player_relation (+0x284c8) already records the gap: 'Two sibling int[8] blocks at +0x28488 and +0x284a8 are zeroed in the same loop and are not yet named.'
findings.proposed: int32_t ai_intel_seen_count[8]; // per-OTHER-PLAYER sighting counter. Incremented once per llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building call, after the same-owner early-out, indexed by the sighted object's owner nibble. Zeroed with ai_player_relation at player init.
findings.evidence: 0x004db290 `INC dword ptr [EAX + 0xe96348]`, with EAX built at 0x004db274-0x004db28d as (observer_owner_byte & 0xf) * 0x288fc + (target_class_byte & 0xf) * 4 -- the 0x288fc player stride and a 4-byte element indexed by a player nibble (0..7), i.e. int32_t[8]. 0xe96348 - 0xe6dec0 (player_data base, mh_regions.gen.h line 595) = 0x28488, which lands inside _pad_0x28488[64]. The row direction is derived TWICE and independently: (a) 0x004db472 writes pd[observer].ai_player_relation[other] = -1 and that field is documented '-1 = hostile', so the row player is the one FORMING the opinion; (b) 0x004db48b calls llm_strat_ai_target_list_add with EAX = the same nibble, and that function appends to pd[EAX].ai_target_list (0xe930ec = +0x2522c), i.e. the row player owns the target list. Reached only after 0x004db26e returns when the two nibbles are equal, so the diagonal is never incremented. NOTE the sibling +0x284a8 (finding -2) is the flag half of the same table.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v191) as proposed, name and type unchanged. Verified independently against a freshly exported listing before applying: the player stride really is 0x288fc (the shift/add chain at 0x004db274-0x004db288 computes 2556 + 2556*64 = 166140), the column really is a nibble scaled by 4 (SHL EBX,0x2 then LEA EAX,[EDX + EBX*0x1]), and the row really is the OBSERVER (ESI = [EBP-0xc] = the EDX parameter, masked at 0x004db264). A STRUCTURAL CONFIRMATION THE FINDING DID NOT CLAIM, and it is the strongest evidence here: +0x28488 and +0x284a8 sit exactly 0x20 apart and immediately precede ai_player_relation, which was ALREADY typed int[8] -- three consecutive int[8] per-opponent blocks, which is precisely what two int[8] arrays at those offsets predict. One correction folded into the field comment rather than the name: the finding implied both arrays sit under the same gate; the seen COUNT is incremented before the `TEST byte ptr [EBP-0xc],0x40` at 0x004db296, so only the FLAGS half is gated.

findings.current: UNNAMED -- the second half of the same `uint8_t _pad_0x28488[64]` blob as finding -1.
findings.proposed: int32_t ai_intel_flags[8]; // per-OTHER-PLAYER intel bitset, only the LOW BYTE is ever set: 0x1 = a building of theirs has been sighted, 0x2 = a MINE sighted, 0x4 = a TURRET sighted, 0x8 = the sighted building is within ai_expand_gate_value of my ai_home_tile, 0x10 = a MOTHER building sighted.
findings.evidence: Five writes in llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building, all `OR byte ptr [<row> + <col>*4 + 0xe96368]` and all under the observer_owner_byte & 0x40 test at 0x004db296: 0x004db2a0 |= 0x1 (unconditional inside the branch); 0x004db2e8 |= 0x2 when Building[building_id].type == race_mine_type(pd[row].is_alien_race) (2 alien / 0x16 human, matching BLDG_TYPE_A_MINE/H_MINE in ai_state.h); 0x004db346 |= 0x4 when the type == 5/0x19 = A_TURRET/H_TURRET; 0x004db3a4 |= 0x10 when the type == 6/0x1a (a THIRD race-paired member, the cfg E_BUILDING MOTHER pair per Ghidra's own decompile which renders these three comparisons as A_MINE/H_MINE, A_TURRET/H_TURRET, A_MOTHER/H_MOTHER); 0x004db432 |= 0x8 when llm_strat_toroidal_dist_sq(pd[row].ai_home_tile_x, ai_home_tile_y, buildings[row][building_id].x, .y) < pd[row].ai_expand_gate_value^2. Element width is confirmed INDEPENDENTLY of the stride-4 indexing by the SECOND referrer llm_strat_ai_recompute_shortage_state @0x004e853f, which reads `dword ptr [EAX + EBX*0x4 + 0xe96368]` (0x004e85a0) and stores a full `dword ... ,0x0` (0x004e85cd) -- so int32_t[8] with only the low byte carrying bits, not uint8_t[32].
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v191) as proposed. All five OR sites confirmed at the cited addresses with the cited bit values (0x1/0x2/0x4/0x10/0x8), all inside the 0x40 gate. The int[8]-not-byte[32] argument was re-checked at its independent source and holds: llm_strat_ai_recompute_shortage_state compares `dword ptr [EAX + EBX*0x4 + 0xe96368]` at 0x004e85a0 and clears a full dword at 0x004e85cd, so the width does not rest on the stride-4 indexing in the function under translation. Ghidra had these as single `undefined` bytes; they are now int[8] with the derivation in the field comment.

findings.evidence: 0x004db45c `CMP dword ptr [0x00e58350],0x0` (_G_LLM_STRAT_AI_FOREIGN_BLDG_CHANGE_FLAG) / JNZ to 0x004db472; the fall-through path at 0x004db465-0x004db470 skips when the two nibbles are equal or when the existing relation is non-zero; 0x004db472 `MOV dword ptr [EAX + 0xe96388],0xffffffff` where 0xe96388 - 0xe6dec0 = 0x284c8 = ai_player_relation, whose committed field comment is 'diplomatic relation toward each player index 0..7: +1 = self/friendly, -1 = hostile'. findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v191), and the finding was right that nothing invalidates a path cache -- 0x004db472 is `MOV dword ptr [EAX + 0xe96388],0xffffffff` into ai_player_relation, gated on _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_FOREIGN_BLDG_CHANGE_FLAG at 0x004db45c with the fall-through skipping on same-nibble or non-zero relation, exactly as described. The replacement plate goes further than the finding proposed: it also records the tail call to llm_strat_ai_target_list_add, the same-owner early-out, and -- deliberately -- the UNSETTLED building_id ambiguity the session declined to resolve, so that whoever next reads this function meets the open question in the plate rather than rediscovering it. conf:high added.

findings.current: void __watcall llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building(int building_id EAX, uint observer_owner_byte EDX, uint unit_id EBX, uint target_class_byte ECX) -- FOUR register params and NO stack param, so Ghidra's implied purge is 0.
findings.proposed: Add a FIFTH parameter, passed on the STACK at [EBP+0x8], so the committed purge becomes 4 and matches the body's own `RET 0x4`. Suggested: `void __watcall llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building(int building_id EAX, uint observer_owner_byte EDX, uint unit_id EBX, uint target_class_byte ECX, int victim_destroyed /*stack*/)`. The param is NEVER READ by the callee -- name it for what the callers compute, and consider a plate line saying it is ignored.
findings.evidence:
THREE independent derivations, none of them a re-read of the Ghidra prototype.
(1) THE CALLEE'S OWN EPILOGUE. 0x004db496 is `RET 0x4` (bytes c2 04 00). tools/data/dll_call_protos.json already records this as purge=4 vs purge_expected=0 and marks the function `status: stack_purge_mismatch`, which is why the generated interop layer emits `MH_UNAVAILABLE__prototype_contradicts_the_functions_own_RET` at mh_calls.gen.h:2444 and a `static_assert(false, ...)` for MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building at mh_export.gen.h:15307. The function therefore cannot be called OR shadowed from the DLL until this is fixed.
(2) BOTH CALL SITES PUSH ONE DWORD AND NEITHER CLEANS IT. Disassembled independently with capstone straight out of F:\games\mh_en\mh_en_clean.bak.exe (md5 b3b389e8eb228638de8dbbc5c228118b == the Ghidra /eng/mh.exe), not from any export:
  llm_strat_bldg_kill_credit  0x0044caa4 `push dword ptr [ebp-0x34]` -> 0x0044cab9 `call 0x4db22f` -> 0x0044cabe `lea esp,[ebp-0x10]`  (no `add esp,4`)
  llm_strat_unit_kill_credit  0x0044cdee `push dword ptr [ebp-0x3c]` -> 0x0044ce03 `call 0x4db22f` -> 0x0044ce08 `lea esp,[ebp-0x10]`  (no `add esp,4`)
The push sits between the FP compare and the EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX marshalling, i.e. it is the 5th argument in Watcom order, and the callee purges it. Caller and callee agree at 4 bytes.
(3) WHAT THE VALUE IS. Both callers compute the same 0/1 flag immediately before pushing it: bldg site 0x0044ca83 `fld qword [eax+0xc3d2c1]` / 0x0044ca89 `fcomp qword [edx+0xc3d2b9]` / fnstsw / sahf / `jb` -> 0 else 1. With buildings base 0x00c3d2a0 (mh_regions.gen.h:527) and stride 0x111, those are map::object::building +0x21 `pending_damage` and +0x19 `energy`, so the flag is `pending_damage >= energy` -- 'this hit destroys the victim'. The unit caller has the identical shape against the unit record (0x0044cdd3 `fcomp qword [edx+0xdd8c60]`).
THE CALLEE NEVER READS IT: disassembling all 0x26a bytes of the body from the same clean exe gives ZERO `[ebp + <positive>]` operands and ZERO `[esp + ...]` operands, so the fifth argument is purged and discarded. Do not let that tempt anyone to drop it from the prototype -- the purge is what the callers depend on.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v193) with the proposed shape and the proposed name -- five params, the fifth `int victim_destroyed` at Stack[0x4]:4 -- committed through commit_prototypes.py's OVERRIDE mode (AUTO cannot fire: it refuses any function whose terminating instruction is `RET n`). TWO CORRECTIONS to the derivation, neither of which changes the conclusion. (1) THE CALLER-SIDE ARGUMENT AS WRITTEN IS NOT EVIDENCE. The finding leans on 'neither call site cleans it (no add esp,4)'. Both callers restore the stack with `LEA ESP,[EBP + -0x10]` (0x0044cabe and 0x0044ce08), a frame-pointer restore that absorbs an uncleaned push identically whether or not the callee purged -- so its absence proves nothing. What actually carries the caller half is that each site PUSHes exactly one dword immediately before the CALL with nothing pushed after it (0x0044caa4, 0x0044cdee), and the purge is settled on its own by the callee's `RET 0x4` at 0x004db496, re-read from a freshly exported listing. (2) THE UNIT CALL SITE'S FIELDS WERE COMPUTED OFF THE WRONG BASE. The finding cited `fcomp qword [edx+0xdd8c60]` and then asserted 'identical shape' without naming a field -- the one claim in it with no offset arithmetic. The units region base is 0x00dd8c48 (mh_regions.gen.h:540), not 0xdd8c60, so the compared fields are unit +0x20 and +0x18, which docs/structs.md gives as pending_damage and energy. That is the same predicate the building site computes (+0x21 vs +0x19 off buildings base 0x00c3d2a0, and THAT half of the finding was correct as written), so `victim_destroyed` survives -- but on a derivation the finding did not supply. Independently re-verified before applying: `RET 0x4` at 0x004db496; ZERO positive [EBP+...] or [ESP+...] operands anywhere in the 0x26a-byte body, so the parameter really is purged and discarded; both call sites' JC-to-0/else-1 flag shape. After the check-in, mh_dump_call_protos re-derives the entry as `status: ok` with purge 4 == frame_bytes 4 (was stack_purge_mismatch), and the generated headers went from MH_UNAVAILABLE__prototype_contradicts_the_functions_own_RET / static_assert(false) to a real inline callable (mh_calls.gen.h:1329, shape void|callee|EAX|EDX|EBX|ECX|S4) and a working MH_EXPORT_REPLACE -- which is what unblocks AI1B layer 0. Also applied, from this finding's own suggestion: a plate paragraph recording that the fifth parameter is never read and is in the signature only because the callers depend on the purge, so nobody later 'tidies' it away. Gate: build + aitest 278/0 + callstest 930/0 + exportstest 592/0 + lint_repo PASS.

findings.evidence: THE CALL SITE, 0x004db24e-0x004db259 in llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building (tmp/decomp_ai/llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building_004db22f.asm): `MOV EDX,EBX` (EBX holds the caller's `unit_id` parameter, spilled to [EBP-0x10] at 0x004db246), `MOV EAX,ECX` (ECX holds the packed target ref), `CALL 0x004d45c0`, then `TEST EAX,EAX / JZ` -- so EAX and EDX in, a full-dword truth value out, and no argument is pushed. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DERIVATION: dll_call_protos.json already reports `purge: 0` / `cleanup: callee` for the VA from the function's own terminator, which rules out any stack parameter without reference to the call site. THIRD: the sibling per-unit predicates in the same address neighbourhood carry exactly this committed shape -- llm_strat_unit_get_sight @0x004d4888 `(uint32_t unit_ref EAX, int32_t unit_index EDX)`, llm_strat_unit_has_aa_weapon @0x004d7311 and llm_strat_unit_has_ground_weapon @0x004d7377, all `s_u32_EAX_EDX` / `s_u8_EAX_EDX` in mh_calls.gen.h:1254/1293/1294. CAVEAT ON THE RETURN WIDTH, stated rather than guessed: the caller's `TEST EAX,EAX` proves it consumes 32 bits, but whether the callee sets all 32 (int32_t) or only AL (uint8_t, like its neighbour get_sight) cannot be read off the call site -- derive it from the body when committing. WHY THIS BLOCKS: the call is not decorative. When it returns non-zero the caller rewrites ECX to `(ECX & 0xf) | 0x20` at 0x004db25b-0x004db25e, and ECX is passed unmodified as the 4th (`owner_class`, ECX) argument of llm_strat_ai_target_list_add at 0x004db48b. So the aircraft result is OBSERVABLE in the sighting record the function appends, and a translation that omitted the call would write a different byte.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v194) as `int32_t __watcall llm_strat_unit_is_aircraft(uint32_t unit_ref EAX, int32_t unit_index EDX)` via commit_prototypes AUTO. THE FINDING LEFT THE RETURN WIDTH OPEN and asked for it to be derived from the body; the body was exported and settles it as int32_t, NOT uint8_t: the function has exactly two exits, `MOV EAX,0x1` at 0x004d464f and `XOR EAX,EAX` at 0x004d4655, both writing the full dword -- so it matches llm_strat_unit_has_aa_weapon / _has_ground_weapon (int32_t) rather than llm_strat_unit_get_sight (uint8_t), which is the sibling the finding hedged toward. A THIRD DERIVATION OF THE PARAMETERS, from the CALLEE side, which the finding did not have (it argued only from the call site and the siblings): 0x004d45d2 `AND EAX,0xf` then `IMUL EAX,EAX,0x5b04`, and 0x004d45db `IMUL EDX,EDX,0xe9` -- 0x5b04 / 0xe9 == 100 exactly, i.e. a 100-unit-per-player table of 233-byte records at 0xdd8c4a, so EAX really is the owner-carrying ref and EDX the unit index within that owner. ANSWERING THE FINDING'S SECOND QUESTION (whether it writes anything, which a shadow arm needs before it may run this outward for real): IT WRITES NOTHING. The whole 0x98-byte body is the entry stack probe, the two index computations, a MOVZX of a 16-bit unit type, ten CMPs of `dword ptr [type*575 + 0xe4a176]` against the contiguous set 0x0f..0x18, and the two EAX exits -- no store to memory at all. Also worth knowing at the call site: 0x004d45ca `TEST AL,0x40 / JNZ` returns 0 immediately for a ref with the 0x40 (building) bit set. Listing exported to tmp/decomp_ai/llm_strat_unit_is_aircraft_004d45c0.asm as requested; the function is now emitted as a real callable in mh_calls.gen.h:1249 and is exportable in mh_export.gen.h.

findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v194), BUT THE CORRECTION IS MUCH LARGER THAN THE FINDING ASKED FOR, and the extra part is the load-bearing bit. The finding proposed amending 'two reads' to 'three reads' and adding the distance semantic. Re-deriving from scratch instead of taking the count on trust: an instruction-level sweep of all 252238 instructions in the image for the little-endian dword 0x00e7df0c -- independent of Ghidra's reference manager, which is the documented blind spot -- returns EIGHT sites, not three: SIX READS (0x004db3c2 register_visible_building; 0x004e42e3 scan_construction_sites; 0x004e4af7 and 0x004e4d0c expand_adjacent_mine_relay; 0x004e79f9 and 0x004e7a4f group_form_perimeter_patrol) and TWO WRITES (0x004e8ccc and 0x004e8cd4, both in llm_strat_ai_player_tick). SO THE COMMENT'S CENTRAL CLAIM -- 'NO WRITER anywhere in the binary, which would make both expansion paths dead on a fresh game' -- IS FALSE, and the field has a producer that runs once per player per AI tick: `gate = trunc(sqrt(llm_strat_bldg_max_defense_radius_sq(player, ai_home_tile_x, ai_home_tile_y)))`, or the constant 5 on the arm where pd[player].ai_score_cat_1 == 0 (`CMP dword ptr [ECX + 0xe96568],0x0` at 0x004e8c93; FUN_004da9f0 is the domain-checked FSQRT wrapper, FTST/SAHF then FSQRT at 0x004daa1f). That producer also confirms the finding's semantic claim from the WRITE side rather than the read side: a value derived by square-rooting a *_radius_sq is a RADIUS IN TILES, which is exactly how 0x004db3c2 (squares it back with IMUL EAX,EAX against llm_strat_toroidal_dist_sq), 0x004e4d0c (radius+5 around ai_home_tile) and the two perimeter-patrol sites (scaled by the quadrant unit vectors) use it. The field comment was rewritten to record all eight sites, the producer, and the fact that the previous text was wrong. NOT DONE, deliberately, and left as an open question for the conductor: _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_EXPAND_MIN_TICKS (0x00669364) is by the same evidence a minimum RADIUS and not a tick count, and the field's own name says 'gate_value' where 'radius' would now be defensible -- both are renames that ripple into generated headers and prose, so an unattended prep session should not make them.

findings.current: Committed as `cc: "__custumocall"` with CALLER cleanup, so tools/data/dll_call_protos.json derives `purge_expected: 0` while the function's own terminator purges 4, and the VA carries `status: "stack_purge_mismatch"` -- the same class of defect that made llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building un-callable and un-shadowable until EN v193 fixed it.
findings.proposed: Recommit with CALLEE cleanup (the `__watcall` recipe in the mh-toolchain skill; one uint stack parameter, void return) so purge_expected becomes 4 and the status reads `ok`. LOW PRIORITY / COSMETIC: nothing in the DLL calls this function and nothing will -- it is the inert Watcom stack probe every Watcom prologue in the image opens with, and translations deliberately do not reproduce it. Queued only because it is a concrete, checkable DB correction, and it is the one mismatch a batch session meets at the head of every single AI listing.
findings.evidence: TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS THAT THE CALLEE CLEANS UP. (1) dll_call_protos.json reads `purge: 4` for the VA straight off the function's own RET imm16, against `purge_expected: 0` computed from the committed caller-cleanup convention -- the two disagree by exactly the one declared 4-byte stack parameter. (2) The call sites do not adjust ESP: in tmp/decomp_ai/llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building_004db22f.asm the sequence is 0x004db232 `PUSH 0x30`, 0x004db237 `CALL 0x004cf46f`, 0x004db23c `PUSH ESI` -- no `ADD ESP,4` between the call and the next stack use, which is only correct if the callee purged the argument. The identical shape opens every Watcom function in the cluster (e.g. llm_strat_ai_queue_release_order @0x004dbf36 `PUSH 0x2c` / CALL / `PUSH ESI`).
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-02 (EN v194) but with a DIFFERENT CONVENTION THAN THE FINDING SUGGESTED. The finding said to recommit 'with CALLEE cleanup (the __watcall recipe ...; one uint stack parameter, void return)'; __watcall is the wrong instrument here, because __watcall passes in registers and this function's single argument is genuinely on the STACK (`XCHG dword ptr [ESP + 0x4],EAX` at 0x004cf46f). The convention that means 'stack args, callee pops' is __stdcall, and that is what was committed, via a commit_prototypes OVERRIDE block: `void __stdcall assert_stack_capacity(uint size)`, dynamic storage, which places size at Stack[0x4] exactly as the custom storage did. ONE FACT THE FINDING MISSED, and it lowers the risk of the change to nil: Ghidra's stackPurgeSize for this function was ALREADY 4 and already valid -- only the convention NAME was custom (__custumocall), and dump_call_protos derives `cleanup` from the convention's extrapop, not from the purge, which is why the two disagreed. So nothing about how Ghidra models the 2225 call sites changed; only the derived status did. Verified after the fact: dll_call_protos.json now reads status `ok` / cleanup `callee` / purge 4 for the VA, and the image-wide stack_purge_mismatch count fell from 14 to 13. Side effect worth naming against the finding's 'nothing in the DLL calls this and nothing will': it is now emitted as an entry-thunk target in mh_export.gen.h (shape e_void_S4__callee), i.e. replaceable, not merely callable. exportstest and callstest were rebuilt and re-run green over the regenerated headers.

findings.proposed: void __watcall llm_strat_ai_bldg_register_visible_building(int victim_index EAX, uint victim_ref EDX, uint aggressor_unit_index EBX, uint aggressor_ref ECX, int victim_destroyed Stack[0x4]:4). Nothing about the STORAGE or the TYPES changes -- the correction is entirely in the four names and in what they let a reader conclude. Concretely: param 2 is the DAMAGED object's packed ref (owner nibble | 0x40 building / | 0x80 unit), which is why the `TEST byte ptr [EBP-0xc],0x40` at 0x004db296 means 'the damaged object is a BUILDING' and not anything about an observer; param 4 is the AGGRESSOR's packed ref, which is why `TEST CL,0x80` at 0x004db249 gates the llm_strat_unit_is_aircraft call; param 3 is the aggressor's unit index; param 1 is the victim's index in ITS OWN roster (buildings[] or units[] depending on the ref kind). The row of all three per-opponent tables is therefore the DAMAGED player and the column is the AGGRESSOR.

findings.current: Both field comments (applied EN v191, and they are otherwise excellent) frame the table as SIGHTING: ai_intel_seen_count is 'AI per-OTHER-PLAYER sighting counter, indexed by the SIGHTED object's owner nibble ... ROW = the OBSERVING player', and ai_intel_flags reads '0x1 = a building of theirs has been sighted', '0x2 = a MINE', '0x4 = a TURRET', '0x10 = a MOTHER', '0x8 = the sighted building lies within ai_expand_gate_value of the observer's ai_home_tile'.
findings.proposed:
Keep the row/column DIRECTION -- it is right, the row really is the player whose table it is -- and correct what the column and the bits MEAN. With PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP, [EBP+0x8] is Stack[0x4], so [EBP+0x10] is Stack[0xc] and [EBP+0x14] is Stack[0x10]. findings.evidence:
MECHANISM, read off the decompile of llm_strat_ai_bldg_queue_handle_recruit_state @0x004e80ef (EN v206). The function branches on the credit and the two arms differ in whether ANY resource moves:
  * credit > 0 -- the FREE arm. Calls llm_strat_order_recruit_unit_enqueue(unit_type, player), then `credit -= _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_CFG_PROMO_ADD` (SUB @0x004e8153), then sets |= 0xc0 on the queue entry. NO llm_strat_econ_track_unit_resource_spend call and NO resource_spent movement anywhere in this arm. The unit is enqueued without being paid for.
  * credit <= 0 -- the PAYING arm. Calls llm_strat_bldg_order_repair_start_enqueue(player, producer, unit_type) [misnamed; it starts production -- finding -1922-10], then llm_strat_econ_track_unit_resource_spend(player, unit_type), then a four-iteration loop `resource_spent[j+1] -= queue_entry.reserved[j]` for j=0..3, then `credit += _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_CFG_PROMO_SUB` (ADD @0x004e81cd), then status |= 0x80.
So PAYING EARNS credit and the credit BUYS a free unit. Both keys default to 1 (get-data 0x00669390 = 0x1, 0x00669394 = 0x1) and the field initialises to 0 (0x004dcecf, 0x004dd5f8), so with stock values the AI alternates strictly pay / free / pay / free -- a 50% discount. AI.SCR can retune both ends independently. This matches the user's report (2026-08-03) that an AI player builds far cheaper than a human, especially early.
PREVIOUS EVIDENCE, unchanged: the keyword-table derivation of nPromoAdd/nPromoSub is in finding -7 (@0x0066951c -> 0x00669390 'nPromoAdd', @0x00669528 -> 0x00669394 'nPromoSub').
STILL NOT SETTLED, and deliberately not asserted:
  (a) Whether the free arm is also INSTANT. Not visible here -- it is a property of llm_strat_order_recruit_unit_enqueue versus the paying order path, and neither was opened.
  (b) What `resource_spent` really is. The paying arm DECREMENTS it, which does not fit a 'total spent' tally; it reads more like a stock or a reservation pool. This matters to the wording above: if it is a stock, the free arm is free; if it is a reservation ledger, the free arm instead never releases the reservation. Either way NO resources move in the free arm, which is what the name ai_promo_credit rests on. Note this is the same field as finding -1731-2, which is already queued to be reshaped -- settle that one first.
  (c) The ADD/SUB CROSSING, worth its own look during the apply: the global named PROMO_ADD is used in a SUBTRACT and PROMO_SUB in an ADD. Either the two Ghidra names are swapped against their AI.SCR keys, or the keys are named from the granting side's point of view. Both default to 1, so the VALUES cannot distinguish the two readings -- it needs the AI.SCR loader or a non-default script.
findings.resolution:
APPLIED IN FULL, name and mechanism both. Re-derived from a freshly exported listing (tmp/decomp_ai/llm_strat_ai_bldg_queue_handle_recruit_state_004e80ef.asm, EN v213) and every mechanical claim held: CMP dword[EBX+0xe7e414],0 / JLE @0x004e8136 is SIGNED; the fall-through arm issues llm_strat_order_recruit_unit_enqueue and does SUB [EBX+0xe7e414],PROMO_ADD @0x004e8153 with OR 0xc0, and contains no econ call and no resource_spent touch at all; the JLE arm calls 0x0046db58 with EAX=player / EDX=producer / EBX=unit_type, then econ_track, then the four-iteration SUB [EAX+0xe7df14],reserved[j] loop @0x004e818e-0x004e819f, then ADD [EAX+0xe7e414],PROMO_SUB @0x004e81cd with OR 0x80. The base arithmetic (stride 166140 = 65*2556) resolves 0xe7e414 to player_data+0x10554 identically in both arms.

THE FINDING'S OWN UNCERTAINTY (c) IS NOW CLOSED, and it was the one that could have caused a wrong rename. It worried the two Ghidra global names might be SWAPPED against their AI.SCR keys, since PROMO_ADD is used in a SUB and PROMO_SUB in an ADD, and noted the values (both 1) cannot tell the readings apart. Settled by reading the keyword table directly rather than by adjacency: the table is at 0x006693b4, 12-byte rows {int kind; void *target; char *name} with KIND FIRST (1=int, 2=float), and row @0x0066951c is {1, 0x00669390, "nPromoAdd"} while @0x00669528 is {1, 0x00669394, "nPromoSub"} -- a direct pointer, no swap. TYPES. 0x01013040 is written by `MOV dword ptr [0x01013040],EBX` @0x004e537a and @0x004e5386, incremented by `INC dword ptr` @0x004e5396 and read by `CMP EAX,dword ptr` @0x004e5473 -- a 4-byte integer at all five sites (the fifth is llm_strat_ai_mine_portfolio_rebalance's read @0x004e35ab; find-cross-references returns exactly those five and nothing else). 0x00e0e468: element size 4 from `FILD dword ptr [EBX + EAX*0x4 + 0xe0e468]` @0x004e389e; per-player stride 40 from EBX = player*40 (SHL/LEA @0x004e3891-@0x004e3899) AND, independently and from a different function, from llm_unit_can_afford_resources' `player_id * 0x28 + Unit[t].resource[i].id * 4` @0x004e23f6; extent 320 bytes from the save block table (tools/data/save_block_table.json, two entries at 0x00e0e468 of 320), which divided by the 40-byte stride gives exactly 8 players -- the same MAX_PLAYERS every other per-player array here uses. 10 int slots per player also matches llm_strat_storage_stats, whose two parallel columns the AI divides this array into are int[10].

findings.proposed: Rewrite the plate around the LAST-candidate gate, the built_flags bit, the empty-slot-does-not-consume-budget rule, and the caller-derived constructive purpose.
findings.evidence: MECHANICAL, all inside the body. TWO DISTINCT FRAME SLOTS. The winner lives in [EBP-0x10] (MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0x10],ESI @0x004e4e6f with ESI = 0xffffffff; MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0x10],EBX @0x004e4efc) with the running best distance in ESI (MOV ESI,EAX @0x004e4eff). The LAST evaluated distance lives in [EBP-0x14] (MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0x14],EAX @0x004e4ef1), and it is stored on EVERY evaluated candidate -- before the TEST EAX,EAX @0x004e4ef4 and the CMP EAX,ESI @0x004e4ef8 that decide whether that candidate wins. The final gate is CMP dword ptr [EBP + -0x14],0xf / JA @0x004e4f07-0x004e4f0b, i.e. it reads the LAST slot, and only the JA path reaches MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP + -0x10] @0x004e4f17. The encodings confirm the two slots are distinct rather than a display artifact: 8945ec / 837dec0f address EBP-0x14, 895df0 / 8b45f0 address EBP-0x10. Consequence: the roster's genuine nearest match is discarded whenever the LAST candidate examined happened to be within 0xf. FLAG: TEST byte ptr [EAX + 0xc3d2a4],0x1 @0x004e4eca. 0xc3d2a4 = buildings + 4 = map::object::building.built_flags, whose own field comment says bit 0x1 = connected/reached (set by llm_bldg_set_connected_flag). It is NOT a plane: the body's complete set of absolutes is {0xc3d2a0, 0xc3d2a2, 0xc3d2a4, 0xc3d363, 0xc3d364, 0x00669f90 llm_strat_toroidal_dist_sq, 0x004cf46f assert_stack_capacity, 0x004e419e epilogue} -- no 0x01013040/0x01013044 and no other data address at all. EMPTY SLOTS: CMP word ptr [EAX + 0xc3d2a2],0x0 / JZ 0x004e4f02 @0x004e4ec0-0x004e4ec8 jumps PAST the DEC ECX at 0x004e4f01, so a hole does not consume the live-count budget; a building that is live but unflagged does consume it (JZ 0x004e4f01 @0x004e4ed1). NO-CANDIDATE CASE: [EBP-0x14] lies in the SUB ESP,0x8 region @0x004e4e64 and is never initialised, so a walk that evaluates nothing reads indeterminate stack. Harmless: [EBP-0x10] is still the -1 from @0x004e4e6f, so BOTH branches return -1. SECOND DERIVATION, THE CALL SITE. ReVA find-cross-references reports exactly ONE reference in the image, from llm_strat_ai_plan_turret_upgrade @0x004e500c. CMP EAX,-0x1 / JZ 0x004e513a @0x004e5011 abandons the candidate on -1; otherwise the index is scaled by the 273-byte roster stride (SHL 4 / ADD / SHL 4 / ADD @0x004e5024-0x004e502c) and used to read buildings[player][idx].y @0x004e502e, which is pushed with .x into llm_strat_tile_midpoint_wrapped. So the found building is a CONNECTION PARTNER to bridge toward, not a too-close duplicate to veto. The already-verified C++ of that caller (src/mh_dll/libmh/ai/ai_turret_plan.cpp:57-64) encodes the same use.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-03 (EN v213) as a full plate replacement, and the applied text says MORE than the finding proposed in two places. (1) The finding called the gate an error; the plate now also carries the CONSEQUENCE in the form a reimplementer needs -- 'a genuine nearest match is returned as -1 whenever some later, unrelated building came out within 0xf' plus an explicit 'reproduce this verbatim', because the natural fix (test the BEST distance) is precisely the wrong thing to do here. (2) The no-candidate case was re-derived rather than restated: [EBP-0x14] really is uninitialised on that path, but it CANNOT change the result, because [EBP-0x10] still holds -1 and both branches return -1. That is why this stayed a plate correction and did not become a translation hazard. WHAT DIFFERS FROM MY OWN FIRST READING: nothing about the gate, but I initially expected the flagged bit to be the AI's connectivity scratch plane, because both ai_state.h and the tracker's AI1B progress block say so. It is not -- the body's complete absolute set contains no 0x01013040/44, and the bit is the roster record's own built_flags 0x1. The two out-of-Ghidra copies of that error are fixed in the same commit (ai_state.h's comment, and the tracker note when this session's progress block is written); the Ghidra plate never claimed the plane, so there was nothing to correct on that count in the DB. NOT changed: the function name, which is accurate ('flagged' is the built_flags bit), and the tags {sub:buildings, patch:base, patch:shift}, which are about the roster-cap patch surface and are unrelated to the defect.

findings.current: Plate: '... each scanner resets and refills the shared _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_SITE_CANDIDATES[] table, and this function tail-calls llm_strat_ai_sort_site_candidates_by_dist ...'. TWO ERRORS: the scanners do NOT reset the count -- this function does, and it holds the only constant store to it in the image; and the sort is an ordinary CALL, not a tail call. The plate also omits that the three scanners' SECOND argument is passed implicitly in EDX.
findings.proposed: Rewrite the plate so the reset is attributed to this body, the three race-paired type tests and their targets are spelled out, the implicit EDX argument is stated, and the sort is described as an ordinary call.
findings.evidence: RESET: MOV dword ptr [0x00fe5b54],0x0 @0x004e7cfa, in THIS body, before any dispatch. ReVA find-cross-references on _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_SITE_CANDIDATE_COUNT (0x00fe5b54) returns 15 references and exactly ONE plain WRITE -- that one. The three scanners hold only READ and READ_WRITE refs, and every write ref among them is an INC: 0x004e6502 (llm_strat_ai_bldg_scan_resource_site_candidates), 0x004e6673 (llm_strat_ai_bldg_scan_grid_candidates), 0x004e682a (llm_strat_ai_scan_build_site_candidates). None of the three stores a constant, so none of them resets. src/mh_dll/libmh/ai/ai_state.h's ai_store comment already records the scanners as APPEND-ONLY, i.e. the plate contradicted a note derived independently at batch A layer 5. DISPATCH: three race-paired cfg Building.type tests, each selecting its constant from player_data[player].is_alien_race (CMP dword ptr [.. + 0xe7e380],0x0, i.e. player_data +0x104c0, @0x004e7d16 / 0x004e7d5d / 0x004e7d98) and comparing it against Building[building_id].type (IMUL EAX,EDX,0x842 then MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [EAX + 0xd9ec88], @0x004e7d2c-0x004e7d32, @0x004e7d73-0x004e7d79, @0x004e7dae-0x004e7db4): 2 vs 0x16 -> CALL 0x004e6396; 8 vs 0x1c OR 7 vs 0x1b -> CALL 0x004e66a4 (both branches converge on LAB_004e7dbf); otherwise CALL 0x004e6591. IMPLICIT SECOND ARGUMENT: all three scanners carry a committed two-register __watcall prototype (EAX, EDX) but each call site loads only EAX (MOV EAX,EBX @0x004e7d3d / @0x004e7dbf / @0x004e7dc8). EDX still holds this function's own building_id parameter -- the body writes EAX, EBX and ECX only, and the three IMULs READ EDX at 0x004e7d2c, 0x004e7d73 and 0x004e7dae -- so each scanner receives building_id in EDX without any call site setting it. SORT: CALL 0x004e6228 @0x004e7dcf is followed by POP ECX / POP EBX / RET @0x004e7dd4-0x004e7dd6; not a tail call.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-03 (EN v213) as a full plate replacement. Relative to the finding, the applied text adds the per-branch type table (2/0x16 -> resource-site scanner, 8/0x1c or 7/0x1b -> build-site scanner, else grid scanner) with the address of each test, so the dispatch can be checked without re-reading the body, and it states the reset's uniqueness as a counted claim ('the ONLY constant store to that global anywhere in the image') rather than as an assertion about this function alone. WHY IT DIFFERS FROM MY FIRST READING: it does not -- but the ORDER of derivation matters and is worth recording. I read the reset in the body first and would have accepted the old plate's 'each scanner resets' as an additional, harmless truth; what refuted it was going to the scanners' listings and finding INC and only INC, then confirming image-wide with find-cross-references. Had I stopped at the body, the plate would still be wrong and a reimplementation could have omitted the store on the theory that a callee does it. The implicit-EDX note is the other addition: it is not a defect in the old plate so much as a landmine it did not disarm, and it is exactly the kind of thing Ghidra's .c cannot show. NOT changed: the tags. todo:globals IS drained and should go, but removal needs ReVA function-tags mode=remove and it does not block the translation -- queued separately as 2026-08-03-1505-3.

findings.proposed: offset 0x8 `field_0x8` -> `start_col_delta` (X/column delta); offset 0xc `override_val` -> `start_row_delta` (Y/row delta). Field comments on offsets 0x0 and 0x4 also corrected in place (names kept).
findings.evidence: THREE independent sources agree. (1) READ SITES: llm_strat_unit_group_step_ground @0x00483011 reads offset 0x8 at NINE addresses (0x00483700, 0x004837cb, 0x00483a54, 0x00483db1, 0x00483e97, 0x00484126, 0x004844a3, 0x00484589, 0x00484818), so `unused` is false on its face; offset 0xc is read at nine matching addresses (0x004836d7, 0x004837fb, 0x00483a98, 0x00483d85, 0x00483eca, 0x0048416a, 0x00484477, 0x004845bc, 0x0048485c), one per site, always in the same block. (2) THE MASK PAIRING FIXES THE AXIS: each 0x8 read is `ADD EDX,[..+0xa4ecb0]` then `AND EAX,[0x00e15398] ; general.width_mask`, and each 0xc read is `ADD EDX,[..+0xa4ecb4]` then `AND EAX,[0x00e153b0] ; general.height_mask` -- width is the column axis, height the row axis. (3) THE CALLEE'S COMMITTED PROTOTYPE NAMES THEM: both values are pushed into `byte * __cdecl llm_strat_trace_greedy_path(int start_col, int start_row, int mode, int goal_col, int goal_row, int heading)` @0x0066a9ac; __cdecl right-to-left push order at 0x00483693..0x0048370f puts the width-masked (offset 0x8) value in `start_col` and the height-masked (offset 0xc) value in `start_row`. Corroborating: the initializer llm_strat_group_step_heading_table_init @0x00460be3 writes only 0/+1/-1 into both fields -- the value range of a tile step, not of a filler word or an 'override'. Offset 0x4 (`turn_delta`) is pushed verbatim as the callee's `mode` argument and its -1 is the inactive-slot sentinel (the slot loop bound is a fixed 3 at 0x00483668, so the `> -1` test at 0x00483685/0x0048368c is what ends the candidate list, not a count). Offset 0x0 (`cand_facing`) is read ONLY from slot 0 of each heading's 3, compared for equality between two units' headings at 0x004838c0 and switched on ==1/==2/==3 at 0x00483c4c..0x00483caa -- a per-heading path-shape class, not a facing.
findings.resolution: Renamed + recommented in Ghidra (EN check-in this session); mh_structs.gen.h regenerated, so the generated static_asserts now pin `start_col_delta`/`start_row_delta`. Safe to rename because NOTHING in src/ referenced the old field names yet -- llm_strat_unit_group_step_ground is the sole consumer and is not yet translated, which is exactly why the correction was made before its translation rather than after. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, and left as open questions in the field comments: (a) offset 0x4 keeps the name `turn_delta` -- deciding between 'turn delta' and 'path mode' needs llm_strat_trace_greedy_path's own `mode` parameter re-derived, and two sibling symbols (llm_strat_heading_candidate_find_slot's parameter, llm_strat_group_member_find_matching_turn_delta's name) carry the word; (b) offset 0x0 keeps the name `cand_facing` even though the comment now records that the code uses it as a class id, because the class's meaning was not re-derived.

findings.current: tools/data/dll_addr_manifest.json's existing note (added SIM1-G-PREP, 2026-08-20) and sim_state.h's paraphrase of it both state the per-slot byte layout as 'x at slot+0, y at slot+1'.
findings.proposed: The layout is the OPPOSITE: byte+0 = row/y, byte+1 = col/x.
findings.evidence: llm_map_region_route_search's live decompilation (0x004236c2): `*(char*)(_G_LLM_MAP_REGION_ROUTE_CAND_SCRATCH + local_20*2) = (char)local_1c + *(char*)(&_G_LLM_MAP_REGION_ROUTE_STEP_DELTAS + local_20)` writes byte+0 from `(char)local_1c` (the LOW byte of the packed start_region parameter), and the paired store writes byte+1 from `local_1c._1_1_` (the SECOND/HIGH byte of local_1c). start_region is used two lines earlier as a direct flat index into `_G_LLM_MAP_REGION_GRID[0][local_1c & 0xffff]`, and sim_state.h's own established convention for this exact cell-index packing (region_cell_at(x,y) = grid[x*256+y], 'x is the outer index') plus the explicit standing comment elsewhere in sim_state.h ('packed (col<<8)|row -- the SAME packing as every pathtrace_pos element') both put col/x in the HIGH byte and row/y in the LOW byte -- so byte+0 (fed by the LOW byte) is row/y, byte+1 (fed by the HIGH byte) is col/x, the reverse of the existing note. This is NOT a Ghidra database fact (no Ghidra symbol/plate encodes it) so it carries no DB write of its own -- filed here for the audit trail since it directly gated how this slice's map_region_routing translation writes the array; the manifest note and sim_state.h comment are corrected in the same commit as this finding.
findings.resolution: Corrected tools/data/dll_addr_manifest.json's _G_LLM_MAP_REGION_ROUTE_CAND_SCRATCH note and sim_state.h's region_route_cand_scratch comment to state byte+0=row/y, byte+1=col/x, citing this finding. No Ghidra DB write (kind is a doc-only correction, included here only for the audit trail per the batch prompt's re-derive-first rule, not because the driver's check-in gate requires it).

findings.current: park_x: byte@0xdc + reserved_0xdd[3] (undefined padding); park_y: byte@0xe0 + reserved_0xe1[3] (undefined padding)
findings.proposed: UNRESOLVED -- possibly park_x/park_y should be int32_t (4 bytes each), absorbing the adjacent padding, OR the padding is genuinely always zero and the 1-byte fields are correct.
findings.evidence: llm_strat_unit_state_enter_walk_in reads park_x/park_y as FULL 32-BIT DWORD loads (0x004803f9 MOV ECX,dword ptr [row+0xc728a0] = park_y-relative-offset 0xe0; 0x00480418 MOV EBX,dword ptr [row+0xc7289c] = park_x-relative-offset 0xdc), immediately SHL 0x5 and passed to dir_from_to. This dword read spans the declared 1-byte field plus its 3 adjacent "reserved"/padding bytes. The translation (sim_unit_state_enter.cpp) currently reads only the declared byte and zero-extends, which is behaviorally IDENTICAL to the original ONLY IF those padding bytes are always zero at runtime -- not proven either way. reimpl-verify (2026-08-21) flagged this as a suspicion (not a confirmed divergence) since no writer of unit_storage was checked for whether it ever touches 0xdd-0xdf/0xe1-0xe3.
findings.resolution: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-21-1329 (SIM1-G3 third slice), no DB change. map_CreateBuilding (tmp/decomp_sim/map_CreateBuilding_004622cb.c:128-139) is the sole writer and it writes the reserved_0xdd[3]/reserved_0xe1[3] bytes explicitly as (uVar4>>8)/(uVar4>>0x10)/(uVar4>>0x18) of the SAME masked tile coordinate uVar4=(x_b+offset)&general.width_mask. general.width_mask/height_mask are power-of-two-minus-one wrap masks and every valid map fits map_object_unit's byte-typed x/y fields (docs/dead-ends.md already documents "On a 256-tile map height_mask is 0xff" as the standing invariant), so width_mask/height_mask <= 0xff always, uVar4 <= 0xff always, and bits 8-31 of the write are unconditionally zero. The original's full-dword read and the translation's clean byte read are therefore value-identical on every reachable input -- the translation is CONFIRMED CORRECT AS-IS. No struct retype, no translation change. sim_unit_state_enter.h's PARK_X/PARK_Y READ HAZARD note updated to RESOLVED with this derivation.

findings.current: Six pool slots carrying DAT_ auto-labels, reported by R9 as unnamed globals the draft READS.
findings.proposed: They are not value reads and must not be named as globals: they are STRING LITERALS whose ADDRESS is taken. Define them as string data instead; Ghidra then labels them s_/u_, which R9's LISTING_AUTO_READ pattern (DAT|PTR|INT|UINT|UNK|FLOAT|DOUBLE|BYTE|WORD only) does not match.
findings.evidence: The tell is the instruction form: `MOV EDX,0x501438` @0x0048226e and `MOV EDX,0x50143e` @0x004822b9 take the ADDRESS and pass it to utils_concat (0x00482278, 0x004822c3) building a UI message that ends at game_ui_PrintTextMessage @0x004822cd; identically `MOV EDX,0x5014c8` @0x0048d9c1 and `MOV EDX,0x5014ce` @0x0048da0c in llm_strat_production_complete. For the other pair, llm_strat_bldg_completion_dispatch selects between them -- `CMP dword ptr [EAX + 0xcff064],0x2` @0x0047993b, then MOV [EBP-0x54],0x50139a @0x00479944 on equal and 0x50139c @0x0047994d otherwise -- and pushes the choice with 0x005d05f0 ("init\\") and the format string 0x0050139e ("%s%s_%02d%02d.DMP"), i.e. it is the race letter in a base-layout filename. Decoding the bytes gave 'A'/'H' (ASCII, 2 bytes each) and L" ("/L")" (UTF-16, 6 and 4 bytes); after defining, Ghidra read the values back as exactly 'A', 'H', ' (', ')', ' (', ')' -- an independent confirmation of the byte-level decode.
findings.resolution: Defined as data at EN v308: StringDataType at 0x0050139a/0x0050139c, UnicodeDataType at 0x00501438/0x0050143e/0x005014c8/0x005014ce, each with a plate recording the selecting instruction. Relative to the finding, the change is that these were NOT given _G_LLM_ names: inventing a global name for a compiler-emitted string literal would misrepresent it, and defining the data clears R9 on better provenance. apply_annotations.py could not do this -- a dynamic string type has length 0, so its clear-range computes end < start and throws (6 FAILURES in tools/applied/2026-08-22-024841-annotations.partial.json); they were defined by an inline run-script instead. That tool limitation is worth fixing but is not in this session's mandate.

findings.current: R9 and R10 scan the WHOLE exported .c, which includes the hand-written plate comment. A plate whose prose still says `field_0x418` or `DAT_00aee8c1` therefore reports a HARD blocker on a function whose CODE does not read any such thing -- and the blocker does NOT clear when the symbol is named, because the plate text is frozen prose that no rename rewrites.
findings.proposed: Recognise this as a distinct class: split each blocker into a REAL body read vs a stale-plate mention, and fix the second class by REWRITING the plate to use the name the field/global now has.
findings.evidence: Measured over the whole sim set with tmp/prose_check.py (body := everything after the first line that is exactly `{`): of 131 HARD blocker tokens, 69 appear in a function BODY and 62 appear ONLY in plate/header prose. By function: 85 blocked, of which 42 have a real body blocker and 43 are blocked ONLY by stale prose. Cross-check: 46 of the 50 distinct prose-only tokens appear in NO function body anywhere in all 492 listings, i.e. the entity they name is already declared and Ghidra renders the real name everywhere it is actually accessed. Worked example confirmed independently: llm_map_region_find_route's plate says field_0x410/0x414/0x418, while llm_map_region (size 0x420) has declared route_bfs_dist (1040), route_parent (1044) and route_mark (1048) -- written at 0x00423dfa, 0x00423eb2 and 0x00423f88 respectively. Second example: llm_strat_unit_apply_damage's plate names DAT_005012d4 in prose while its code reads only 0x005013d0 (grep: 0 occurrences of 005012d4 in its .asm).
findings.resolution: Applied at EN v311. 49 stale plate comments across 48 functions were rewritten to cite the name the field/global actually has, in three passes (tools/oneoff/2026-08-22-fix-stale-plates*.py; the prose-vs-body splitter that found them is tools/oneoff/2026-08-22-prose-vs-body-split.py). Relative to the finding as raised, three things changed. (1) The fix is a DOCUMENTATION fix, not a way of quieting the check: every target was confirmed already-declared first -- 46 of the 50 distinct prose-only tokens appear in NO function body anywhere across all 492 listings, and the four that do were confirmed per-function. A plate saying `field_0x418` when the field is `route_mark` is actively misleading whatever the checker thinks of it. (2) One plate did not need a token swap but a CORRECTION: llm_strat_refresh_building claimed its no-energy branch sets 'ratio 0, flag field_0x2d=1.0 sentinel'. Both halves are wrong. FLDZ/FCOMP against energy @0x00470610 branches to LAB_00470b26 when energy <= 0, and that block stores 0x0 @0x00470b39 and 0x3ff00000 @0x00470b43 -- one double = 1.0 -- into the single `efficiency` field at +0x29. There is no field at +0x2d; those bytes are efficiency's tail, so the original reading was a split-double misread (docs/dead-ends.md section B). Why a destroyed building gets a full 1.0 multiplier rather than 0 is left UNRESOLVED and now says so in the plate. (3) A TRAP for the next sweep, learned the hard way: pass 2's own replacement text said 'split out of the old reserved_0x4[52]', which the scanner matched, so the rewrite re-created the blocker it had just cleared. Describe a former pad WITHOUT spelling its old identifier. Measured effect: 88 HARD blockers over 87 functions before, 9 over 9 after (405 -> 483 of 492 clear), of which the plate work accounts for the large majority.

findings.current: Four anonymous cfg-prototype fields (field49_0x22f, field33_0x10b, field48_0x6ed, field32_0x269) read by 8 sim functions and ALREADY CONSUMED, unnamed, by five checked-in reimplementation TUs as _unnamed_0x22f / _unnamed_0x10b / _unnamed_0x6ed / _unnamed_0x269.
findings.proposed: Unit.weapon_facing_tolerance (uint), Unit.kill_score (int), Building.per_shot_cost (double), Building.kill_score (int).
findings.evidence: Each name came from the WRITER (the cfg parser), not from the readers alone, and each writer stores a LITERAL that was decoded rather than inferred. weapon_facing_tolerance: cfg_final_unit_Construct @0x004568db stores a byte-widened local that its movement-class switch sets to 4 for ground vehicles and helis and 1 for foot/walker units and planes (raw asm 0x0045683e-0x00456890); the readers test a circular window (target-cur)<=tol || (0x18-tol)<=(target-cur) over a 24-heading circle at 0x004865a7 / 0x00486336 / 0x00486456, and llm_strat_unit_state_attack_unit halves it first (SAR/SUB/SAR @0x004852f6). per_shot_cost: cfg_final_building_Construct writes it as two dwords 0x9999999a @0x00457eb5 and 0x3fb99999 @0x00457ebf = IEEE-754 0.1, unconditionally for every building type; llm_strat_bldg_state_turret_scan spends it out of the tick budget (FCOMP @0x00471b2b, FSUB @0x00471d8f) and _turret_attack spends it scaled (FLD @0x00471e95, FMUL @0x00471e9b). kill_score (both): both kill-credit functions ADD the field to the SAME destination address 0xdd8c70 = units[killer].experience (bldg read @0x0044c81e add @0x0044c824; unit read @0x0044cc4a add @0x0044cc50), and docs/structs.md's existing comment on that destination field already calls the source 'cfg kill_score' -- so the name reuses established project vocabulary rather than inventing one. Writers hardcode 10 (buildings, @0x004570da) and 1 (units, @0x00456551) unconditionally. Independent corroboration: five pre-existing reimplementation TUs in src/mh_dll/mh/sim derived the same semantics from the same disassembly before any of them could see this naming. The apparent 'two reads into two doubles' at field48_0x6ed is a DECOMPILER ARTIFACT, checked and rejected: the .asm copies one 8-byte double via two 32-bit MOVs into ONE stack slot (0x00471ad8/0x00471ae1) and reads that slot twice.
findings.resolution: Applied at EN v309 and rippled through the tree in the same change, per the standing authority that a rename's migration cost is a cost and not a blocker: Ghidra field rename -> mh_dump_struct_layouts -> gen_dll_structs (the four static_asserts on the new names are in mh_structs.gen.h) -> every spelling of the old names updated across 9 src/mh_dll files -> build + run_selftests.py (ASan + plain, 17 suites) + lint_repo all green. The ripple was LARGER than the four fields: naming the turret pads in the same check-in broke `_pad_0x1c` / `_pad_0x25` references in sim_map_create_building.cpp and its selftest, which is how the turret readings got independently corroborated -- that selftest already asserted `+0x1c == cfg.sight` and `+0x25 == 1 (armed)` / `== 0 (unarmed)`, matching cached_sight and resupply_available exactly. One recorded guess was DISPROVED and the prose corrected: sim_map_create_building.h had speculated +0x25 was 'plausibly a paired has-fired-at-least-once flag'; llm_strat_turret_fire @0x0047c0f1 clears it when the resupply countdown at +0x33 reaches 0, tying it to resupply and not to firing. A correction to carry forward, recorded in the field comments: although all four fields live on the per-TYPE cfg record, the parser never varies three of them -- per_shot_cost is 0.1 and the two kill_scores are 10 and 1 for EVERY type, unconditionally. sim_combat_kill_credit.h's banner calling this a 'cfg-defined kill-score' is true of the slot and misleading about the data.

findings.current: Declared gfx_struct_cursor_anim_state[28], spanning 0x00ae4668..0x00ae4828. Five sim functions read what Ghidra renders as `&_G_LLM_CURSOR_ANIM_STATES[0x10].field_0x4`, i.e. inside elements 16+ of that declaration. This is the R10 field_0x4 HARD blocker on llm_strat_unit_get_coords, _calc_fine_axis_pos, _calc_render_fine_y, _calc_interp_pixel_pos and llm_strat_path_make_single_step.
findings.proposed: The array is very likely typed TOO LONG at [28] and should be [16]; elements 16-27 appear to be a separate ~25-entry {int dx; int dy;} per-facing arc-delta table based at 0x00ae4768, which the five readers index by unit.facing_target with stride 8.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic partition, which is exact and currently unexplained by the declared layout: 0x00ae4668 + 16*16 = 0x00ae4768 (the readers' base) and 0x00ae4768 + 25*8 = 0x00ae4830, which is exactly the base of the next declared global _G_LLM_STRAT_BLDG_DONE_FUNCS. The current [28] declaration ends at 0x00ae4828 and leaves an unexplained 8-byte gap before that neighbour. The stride-8 two-int32 access shape does not match gfx_struct_cursor_anim_state (16 bytes, frame/base_frame/last_time-double). Facing range corroboration: llm_strat_unit_update_rotation wraps facing values into [1,24] and llm_strat_dir_from_to is documented as a 1-of-24 compass sector function, so a table indexed by facing needs 25 slots. Reader instructions: 0x0044b1cd/0x0044b1f3, 0x0048c8cf/0x0048c938, 0x0048cd3c, 0x0048ce84, 0x004956fb/0x0049570c, plus the sibling llm_strat_unit_calc_render_axis_pos @0x0048caf8. Ghidra's own .asm auto-comments label the same two addresses INCONSISTENTLY with the .c (field5_0x8/field9_0xc vs frame/field_0x4), which is itself a symptom of a wrong enclosing type. || WRITER SUBSEQUENTLY FOUND, which is what converted this from a held hypothesis into an applied fix. llm_strat_unit_facing_offset_init @0x0045fac0 -- the same boot routine that settled the near-identical _G_LLM_STRAT_DIR_STEP_OFFSET_TABLE extent bug at 0x00ae2d08 -- writes the table directly, and its loop bound is the evidence docs/dead-ends.md demands. Verified by the conductor from the raw bytes, not from a decompiler rendering: 0x0045fadf `83 7D E8 19` = CMP dword ptr [EBP-0x18],0x19 with `FF 45 E8` INC at 0x0045faea, so the index runs to 24; 0x0045fbf2 `C1 E0 03` = SHL EAX,3, the x8 stride; 0x0045fbf5 `89 90 68 47 AE 00` = MOV [EAX+0x00ae4768],EDX and 0x0045fc05 `89 90 6C 47 AE 00` = MOV [EAX+0x00ae476c],EDX, the dx and dy stores. Footprint through index 24 is 0x00ae4768 + 25*8 = 0x00ae4830, landing exactly on _G_LLM_STRAT_BLDG_DONE_FUNCS with no slack. The entries are hardcoded {dx,dy} pairs with both components in {-1,0,1}, chosen by a range-chain on the heading -- the discretised step direction per facing, not a trig table (the init function fills the separate trig table from degree literals further down).
findings.resolution: Applied at EN v312. _G_LLM_CURSOR_ANIM_STATES retyped gfx_struct_cursor_anim_state[28] -> [16], and 0x00ae4768 declared as _G_LLM_STRAT_FACING_STEP_SIGN, llm_vec2i[25]. Two corrections relative to the finding as raised. (1) The old typing was wrong in BOTH directions, not just too long: at [28] it ended at 0x00ae4828, which is 8 bytes SHORT of what the writer actually touches, so it simultaneously mis-typed the neighbour's bytes as 16-byte cursor records and truncated it. (2) The proposal was a NEW {int dx; int dy;} struct; the existing llm_vec2i was reused instead -- it is what the sibling _G_LLM_STRAT_DIR_STEP_OFFSET_TABLE already uses, and inventing a near-duplicate type would have been the wrong call. Slot 0 is allocated but never written (the loop starts at 1), matching llm_strat_unit_update_rotation's [1,24] heading wrap; the plate says so rather than implying 25 live entries. Self-validating outcome: the five blocked readers now decompile as _G_LLM_STRAT_FACING_STEP_SIGN[unit.facing_target].dx/.dy -- the index expression Ghidra recovers on its own is exactly the facing_target the hypothesis predicted, which no part of the retype forced.

findings.resolution: Applied at EN v313 and rippled. apply_annotations.py REFUSED the park_x/park_y edit -- map_object_unit_storage is a PACKED struct and replaceAtOffset would corrupt a packed layout (the tool's own guard, per docs/dead-ends.md); done instead with an explicit delete+insert run-script, back-to-front so ordinals stayed valid, and verified: size unchanged at 244 and exit_tile_x still at +0xe4. Ripple paid in the same change: regenerate, drop the now-pointless store_u32_le() workaround for a plain assignment, RETIRE the sim_storage_dock.h hazard note (it had the causation backwards -- the dword read was right and the committed type was wrong), and fix the selftest's `reserved_0xdd`/`reserved_0xe1` pre-seeds. Two mutation tests were run on the affected checks and THE FIRST ONE EXPOSED A VACUITY IN MY OWN WORK, which is recorded here rather than quietly fixed: (a) narrowing the park_x store to (uint8_t) did NOT turn the paired ld32 'width' checks red -- once the field is int32_t the assignment writes all four bytes regardless, so those checks cannot pin the width and a comment I had just written claiming they did was wrong; it is corrected in place. (b) Swapping park_y's hmask for wmask also did not go red, because C9 used y_b=9 and every y value fitted inside the 0x3f height mask, so the two masks were indistinguishable. Fixed by raising y_b to 70, after which the mutation DOES go red naming the mechanism (`C9 storage.park_y == (y_b+park_offset_y)&hmask  [got 0x49, want 0x09]`) and green on revert. NAME CAVEAT carried into the field comment rather than resolved: interplanetary_capable's mechanism is settled but the designer-facing label is not -- the cfg column is called `ability`, and whether that is a richer bitmask elsewhere was not established. Gate: build + run_selftests.py (ASan + plain, 17 suites) + lint_repo, all green.

findings.resolution:
APPLIED, but NOT the way the finding expected -- the doc was wrong AND creating the type would also have been wrong. What changed: docs/gfx-sprites.md's Structs section no longer claims `gfx_sprite_hdr` is 'applied to _G_LLM_CUR_SPRITE_HDR', and now opens with a box saying explicitly which two of its four entries are real Ghidra types (gfx_sprite_meta, gfx_struct_banki_row) and which two are documented layouts only (gfx_sprite_hdr, gfx_sprite_hdr_v2). No Ghidra type was created and no global was retyped.

RE-DERIVED, confirming the finding's own checks: no `gfx_sprite_hdr` in the DTM (a sweep of getAllDataTypes for 'sprite' returns only cfg_dynamic_struct_Sprite, cfg_static_struct_Sprite, cfg_t_sprite_index, gfx_sprite_meta and its two array types), and _G_LLM_CUR_SPRITE_HDR @0x00603aec is `undefined4`, length 4, value 0 at rest. So the doc's claim was aspirational, not stale -- there is no evidence a type ever existed and was removed.

THE FINDING ASKED 'whether a formal DTM type should exist' AND THE ANSWER IS NO, FOR THIS GLOBAL, ON EVIDENCE THE FINDING DID NOT HAVE. _G_LLM_CUR_SPRITE_HDR is a POINTER variable (22 references: 12 writes, all `MOV [0x00603aec],<reg>` from the seven llm_gfx_draw_sprite* setters and the two cursor drawers -- e.g. 0x004a885e, 0x004a898a, 0x004296e3; and 10 reads, all `MOV ESI,dword ptr [0x00603aec]` inside the blitters). AND IT IS POLYMORPHIC: llm_gfx_blit_sprite_rle_v2 reads the SAME global at 0x0043bc22, where the pointee is the 7-byte gfx_sprite_hdr_v2, not the 14-byte V1 header -- llm_gfx_draw_sprite_v2 @0x004296e3 is what writes it on that path. Typing the global `gfx_sprite_hdr *` would therefore make four V1 blitter reads render correctly and the V2 blitter read render WRONG, with no warning anywhere -- a silently misleading decompile, which is strictly worse than the honest `undefined4` it carries today. That reasoning is now written into the doc so the question does not get re-opened.

WHAT IS STILL AVAILABLE, and is NOT this finding: if these layouts are ever worth DTM types, the place to apply them is the per-function ESI locals inside the blitters that have already branched on the sprite version, never the shared global. That is gfx work with no consumer today and it is deliberately not opened here -- this was a sim-migration PREP session, and the finding's own scope was 'is the doc telling the truth'.

NOTE ON THE OFFSETS: not touched and not in doubt. The finding said they are corroborated by the 2026-08-22 derivation of llm_strat_bldg_sprite_anchor_offset; the doc also records a check of all 6841 retail V1 sprites. Only the 'applied' claim was false.

findings.note: GHIDRA BUG HIT WHILE APPLYING THIS, recorded so the next session does not spend the time: FunctionManager.removeFunction() throws java.util.ConcurrentModificationException on any function carrying TWO OR MORE function tags. Ghidra 12.1.2 FunctionManagerDB.doRemoveFunction iterates `function.getTags()` and calls `function.removeTag(...)` inside that loop (SoftwareModeling-src.zip, ghidra/program/database/function/FunctionManagerDB.java, the 'Remove all tag mappings' block). This project tags nearly everything, so it will recur. Workaround: read the tag names into a python list, removeTag each, THEN removeFunction. Also: a DeleteFunctionCmd that throws part-way leaves the function present with an EMPTY body, which then makes the next attempt look like a different failure -- restore a valid body with setBody() before retrying.

findings.proposed: void __watcall f(void) for all 26.
findings.evidence: TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS. (1) Direct read of all 26 freshly exported .asm listings in tmp/decomp_sim: every one takes its inputs from the two globals _G_LLM_STRAT_CUR_BUILDING (0x00e162dc) and _G_LLM_STRAT_CUR_PLAYER (0x00e58144), and every use of EAX/EDX/EBX is written before it is read -- e.g. llm_strat_power_consume starts `MOVZX EAX,[0x00e58144]` @0x0047045e, llm_strat_add_storage_capacity starts `MOV EAX,[0x00e162dc]` @0x004701d7, llm_strat_bldg_anim_state_port starts `MOV [EBP-0x1c],1` @0x0047870d. ECX is never read in any of the 26. Every one ends in a plain RET (purge 0), so there are no callee-cleaned stack args either. (2) commit_prototypes.py's own decompiler-dataflow derivation, run first as a dry run: 25 of 26 reported `ndec=0 regs=[] vararg=False ret_n=False`, i.e. the decompiler independently infers zero parameters. THE SINGLE DISAGREEMENT, and why it is not a counter-example: llm_strat_add_storage_capacity @0x004701bf reported ndec=2 regs=[EAX,EDX]. Its decompile ends `return CONCAT44(param_2,pmVar1);` -- the Watcom FAKE RETURN idiom already in docs/dead-ends.md, where an `undefined` return type makes the decompiler invent an 8-byte EDX:EAX result and back-propagate EDX as an input parameter. Its listing writes EDX at 0x00470205/0x00470210/0x00470216 before any read and never reads it on entry. Committing `void` removes the invented return and with it the invented parameter.
findings.resolution: APPLIED via tools/commit_prototypes.py with a per-function `override: {conv: __watcall}` block (26/26 committed, 0 flagged, 0 errors; audit copy tools/applied/2026-08-23-015942-prototypes.json). OVERRIDE rather than AUTO because the tool's AUTO path requires at least one register parameter and so cannot express a zero-argument function at all -- that is a gap in the tool, not a doubt about these functions; the derivation above is what the override rests on. Self-verify reported one soft `extraout_` (llm_strat_power_generate), which is the separate R3 item -- see finding 2026-08-23-0149-4. findings.evidence: `extraout_EAX` stands in for `_G_LLM_STRAT_CUR_PLAYER * 0x18`, established by `MOVZX EAX,word ptr [0x00e58144]` @0x004702d3 + `IMUL EAX,EAX,0x18` @0x004702da and never rewritten; the same EAX is the base of the READ `FILD dword ptr [EAX + 0xbf4fc0]` @0x004702fc and the WRITE `FISTP dword ptr [EAX + 0xbf4fc0]` @0x00470313, i.e. a read-modify-write of _G_LLM_STRAT_POWER_STATS[player].generated across `CALL utils_math_trunc` @0x0047030e. utils_math_trunc preserves EAX -- proved by exhaustion over all 11 instructions of its body (0x004d0596-0x004d05b2): PUSH EAX (scratch for FSTCW, released by `LEA ESP,[ESP+8]` @0x004d05ae) / FSTCW / WAIT / PUSH dword[ESP] / MOV byte[ESP+1],0x1f / FLDCW / FRNDINT / FLDCW / WAIT / LEA / RET; writes to EAX = 0, no other GPR named at all, getStackPurgeSize()=0 agreeing with the plain RET. Ghidra cannot express that: `<unaffected>` belongs to the prototype MODEL, and every model in x86watcom.cspec lists EAX as an output pentry. SCOPE MEASURED: of utils_math_trunc's 374 call sites, ~18 hold a value in EAX across the call, in 4 functions -- this one, cfg_final_building_Construct (10, e.g. 0x459302), llm_strat_bldg_get_progress_percent (6, e.g. 0x44a14d), llm_tact_unit_apply_move_offset (0x42c538). Only this one is in the sim set, and it is the ONLY live EAX artifact across all 530 exported sim listings.
findings.resolution:
APPLIED as an ACK plus documentation, deliberately NOT as a cspec change. The mechanism is written into BOTH plates -- llm_strat_power_generate's (what extraout_EAX actually is, with the addresses) and utils_math_trunc's (its full register-preservation contract, since 374 call sites read that plate) -- so no translator is misled. The readiness ack is in tools/data/sim_ready_ack.json, and the real fix is written up as a new section of tasks/tooling.md ('A cspec model for the register-PRESERVING FPU helpers'), deliberately BATCHED with the two cspec items already parked there.

WHY NOT JUST DO IT: a cspec edit is read only at program-open, so it is Ghidra-restart-scoped; a restart drops ReVA mid-session, and re-modelling the decompilation of the whole binary is not a decision an unattended session should take alone. tasks/tooling.md already records this project's posture in as many words -- 'not worth a restart on its own; fold it into the next session that already needs one'. The measured blast radius (4 functions binary-wide, 1 in the sim set) is what makes batching right rather than a dodge.

findings.current: The 14 TICK2 animation callbacks were split two ways with no principle. Seven carried `void (undefined4 player, undefined4 index, uint arg_ebx, uint arg_ecx)`; llm_strat_bldg_anim_state_online_toggle carried `void (void)`. All 14 are installed in _G_LLM_STRAT_BLDG_TICK2_FUNCS by llm_strat_register_bldg_type_callbacks and reached ONLY through the table.
findings.proposed: `void __watcall (undefined4 unused_eax, undefined4 unused_edx, uint unused_ebx, uint unused_ecx)` for all eight -- the seven, plus online_toggle. Two changes: give online_toggle the slots its siblings have, and stop calling the first two `player` and `index`, which they are not.
findings.evidence:
THE NAMES WERE WRONG. The sole dispatch is llm_strat_bldg_tick_animation_state's `CALL dword ptr [EAX + 0xae49c0]` @0x00476437; the three instructions before it are `MOV EAX,[0x00e162dc]` / `MOVZX EAX,word ptr [EAX + 0x2]` / `SHL EAX,0x2` (0x0047642b-0x00476434), so EAX = building_id*4 -- a TABLE INDEX, not a player -- while EDX still holds player*0x6aa4 from `IMUL EDX,EAX,0x6aa4` @0x00476328. No argument is set up at all. Each of the eight is referenced ONLY by PARAM refs from the registrar (helipad: 0x0045f9d5; online_toggle: 0x0045fa02/11/20/2f/3e/4d; etc.) -- there is no direct call anywhere in the image. And an instruction sweep over each body finds NO read of EAX/EBX/ECX/EDX before a write; the bodies take player and index from _G_LLM_STRAT_CUR_PLAYER / _G_LLM_STRAT_CUR_INDEX instead (e.g. helipad @0x004777fc, @0x00477803).

WHY THE SLOTS ARE DECLARED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the bodies FORWARD the incoming EBX/ECX to their llm_strat_bldg_online_* callee, which declares param_3 in EBX and param_4 in ECX. With no declaration the decompiler must invent a name for that forward -- which is exactly why online_toggle carried six `unaff_EBX`/`unaff_ECX` tokens and was R3-blocked while its six identically-shaped siblings were clean. Declaring the slots is also the project's existing precedent for dead Watcom slots (llm_strat_unit_predict_coords_after_delay and llm_strat_bldg_start_special_anim both carry `unused_ebx`/`unused_ecx`).
findings.resolution:
APPLIED to all eight via commit_prototypes.py `override: {conv: __watcall}` (8/8 committed, 0 flagged; audit copy tools/applied/2026-08-23-022225-prototypes.json). MEASURED RESULT, from a fresh lint_annotations.py artifact scan and a fresh whole-domain re-export, not assumed: llm_strat_bldg_anim_state_online_toggle's six R3 tokens are GONE and it is now a clean draft; the other seven stayed clean. Plates updated on online_toggle (whose plate still asserted 'void(void).') and on helipad.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE, and it is the bigger fact here: llm_strat_bldg_register_online (0x004747d6) and its THIRTEEN llm_strat_bldg_online_* handlers all carry `(player AX/EAX, building_index EDX, param_3 EBX, param_4 ECX, double anim_dur Stack[0x4])` where EBX and ECX are never read by the body AND never set by any call site -- so those two parameters are almost certainly not in the original source signature at all (Watcom simply skipped the slots for a 3-argument function whose third argument is a double). Trimming them would clear the last R3 blocker (helipad), but it is a 14-function family decision that cuts across storage modes -- some of the family is on CUSTOM storage, where trimming is safe, and some on DYNAMIC, where it would relocate the stack double -- and it contradicts the `unused_ebx` precedent above, which exists because real parameters follow the dead slots there. That is a convention call about how this project models slot-skipping Watcom signatures, so an unattended session should not take it. Recorded here, in the helipad ack, and in SIM1-BLDGCB's progress instead. A wider count, for whoever takes it: 39 functions in the image declare EBX:4 and ECX:4 parameters that their bodies never read.
