findings.current: The star-system catalog is modelled by TWO overlapping symbols eight bytes apart: a bare hand label `System` at 0x00be1a30 with no array type, and `cfg_final_struct_System[3]` (renamed _G_LLM_CFG_SYSTEMS this session) applied at 0x00be1a38.
findings.proposed: OPEN. The record really starts at 0x00be1a30; the applied array is 8 bytes late and its element type is missing the two leading fields. Re-derive the whole 0x8c layout, then re-apply it at the true base.
findings.evidence: cfg_final_system_Construct (0x0045e473) writes FOUR single-register-displacement scalars, all strided by 0x8c through EDX: [EDX+0xbe1a34] at 0x0045e4a8, [EDX+0xbe1a30] at 0x0045e4bb, [EDX+0xbe1a3c] at 0x0045e4f0 and [EDX+0xbe1a38] at 0x0045e8a8. Two of those (0xbe1a30, 0xbe1a34) are BELOW the applied array's base, and they use the same 0x8c stride as the array -- so they are fields of the same record, not a separate object. The symbol table agrees and shows the split plainly: 0x00be1a30 and 0x00be1a34 carry the bare label `System` with data type `undefined`, while 0x00be1a38 onward is cfg_final_struct_System[3]. Arithmetic closes too: with a base of 0x00be1a30 and a 0x8c stride, four leading dwords plus a 30-entry planets array (0x14 + 30*4 = 0x8c) accounts for every byte, whereas the current type's planets[32] at +0x0c overruns its own 0x8c element by 8. And 30 is exactly what the constructor fills: planet3 plus planets[0..28]. R4b independently reports the same thing from the read side -- llm_ui_main_panel_draw indexes `System` at 0x00be1a30 and 0x00be1a34 with no array type, so Ghidra renders it as pointer arithmetic on a scalar.
findings.resolution: CONFIRMED AND APPLIED 2026-08-24 (EN v345) -- base right, layout hypothesis wrong. The record does start at 0x00be1a30 and the array was 8 bytes late, exactly as this finding said. But its layout reasoning (four leading dwords + planets[30]) is refuted: the record is three leading dwords + planets[32] at +0x0c, i.e. precisely the shape cfg_final_struct_System ALREADY had. Element size 0x8c confirmed; the count is 4, not 3. So no type definition changed and nothing was deleted -- only the placement. Four independent derivations agree: the save/load block moves 0x230 bytes from 0x00be1a30 at four sites (game_SaveGame 0x004472a3, llm_game_load 0x004477d6, llm_cfg_save_final_snapshot 0x00448a94, llm_cfg_load_final_snapshot 0x00448bc6) and 0x230 = 4*0x8c; the corrected array abuts Projects at 0x00be1c60 exactly, where the old placement left 132 bytes unclaimed; cfg_final_system_Construct's raw write displacements resolve to invention@+0x00, name@+0x04, icon@+0x08 and planets[k]@+0x0c+k*4 with k running 0..31; and the cfg parser's own keyword-to-offset table lands on the same four. APPLIED: cleared the misplaced array, deleted the duplicate interior `System` label at 0x00be1a34 and the `_G_LLM_CFG_SYSTEMS` label at 0x00be1a38, applied cfg_final_struct_System[4] at 0x00be1a30, wrote all four field comments and a plate on the global. The hand-named `System` symbol at the true base is now the only name for the object. VERIFICATION THE RETYPE PREDICTED AND DELIVERED: 0x00be1ac4 previously rendered as _G_LLM_CFG_SYSTEMS[1].invention and now renders as System[1].icon (it is the sentinel copy in cfg_ConstructSystems, which makes sense only under the corrected base), and 0x00be1acc moved from [1].icon to System[1].planets[1], the entry planet. The DLL side had independently bound the correct base all along (mh_addrs.gen.h, dll_addr_manifest.json: 0xbe1a30, 4 elements, 0x230) -- only its prose repeated the shifted reading, corrected here. tasks/tooling.md's open item since 2026-08-14 is closed by this; see 2026-08-24-0228-20 for why its proposed `.icon` rename must NOT be done. New docs/dead-ends.md row filed for the class.

findings.addr: tooling: Memory.getBytes(Address, <python bytearray>) in the ReVA PyGhidra runtime
findings.symbol: a byte reader that returns the right COUNT and leaves the buffer zeroed
findings.current: The R4 rule says a boot constant needs its VALUE read out of the image. The obvious inline script is `b = bytearray(n); mem.getBytes(addr, b)`. It returns n -- reporting success -- and every byte reads 0.
findings.proposed: The call is broken, not the data. The Java signature is getBytes(Address, byte[]) and it fills the array in place; a Python bytearray marshals in as a COPY, so the JVM writes somewhere the Python side never sees. Read with mem.getByte(addr.add(i)) instead, or with ReVA's read-memory tool. `jarray` does NOT exist in this runtime (PyGhidra is CPython + JPype, not Jython), so the usual Jython workaround fails.
findings.evidence: Reproduced against a known value: _G_LLM_CONST_SECONDS_PER_HOUR at 0x005000fe must be 3600.0. `mem.getBytes(a, bytearray(8))` returned 8 and printed `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00`; `mem.getByte(a.add(i))` over the same eight addresses printed `00 00 00 00 00 20 ac 40` = 0x40AC200000000000 = 3600.0, and ReVA's read-memory tool agreed. The two readers also differ on a second axis that matters: getByte RAISES MemoryAccessException on an uninitialised block (it did so at 0x008260b4 in .bss), so it distinguishes `zero` from `not present`, which the bytearray path silently conflates.
findings.resolution: APPLIED as docs/dead-ends.md G45, and the two wrong claims it produced this session were corrected in the same commit -- see findings -9 and -10. What gave it away was arithmetic, not suspicion of the tool: four DOUBLE_* globals that are the operands of FMUL/FDIV/FADD read as 0.0, and shipping code does not divide by zero. The control test is one line -- read a KNOWN constant and check it. Recorded because the failure mode is the worst available: not an error, not a refusal, but a plausible self-consistent wrong answer that repeats identically on re-run, and `all zeros` is exactly what an analyst is primed to accept for .bss-looking data.

findings.evidence: llm_tact_unit_owner_tick reads (address of the +0x54 field)[cmd_index * 0xb]: IMUL EAX,cmd_index,0xb @0x00433641 / ADD EAX,row @0x00433645 / CMP byte ptr [EAX+0x826124],0x0 @0x0043365e, and treats 'op != 0 OR this != 0' as slot-occupied. Under the CURRENT +0x55 base that expression is byte +0xa of entry (slot-1) -- the code would be consulting the PREVIOUS slot's spare byte at the current index, which is odd. Under a +0x54 base it is entry `slot`'s own leading flag, which is not odd at all. COUNTER-EVIDENCE, and the reason this is not being applied: the array's far end fits the +0x55 base better. 0x55 + 0x80*0xb = 0x5d5, and the next defined field is field_5d5 at exactly +0x5d5 with no gap; with base +0x54 the array ends at +0x5d4 and leaves a lone unaccounted byte before field_5d5.
findings.resolution: CONFIRMED AND APPLIED 2026-08-24 (EN v345). The queue is based at tact_unit_record+0x54, not +0x55, and the entry is exactly 0xb bytes with NO slack: { byte interrupt_flag; ushort op; ushort arg0..arg3 }. Both models predict the same addresses for every already-documented field, so the decision came from sites that touch the DISPUTED byte, as the finding required. Five agree, all indexing base 0x826124 (unit 0 +0x54) with stride 0xb at ONE index: llm_tact_unit_enqueue_command writes all six fields in one block (0x0042b88f-0x0042b90a); llm_tact_unit_cmd_queue_resubmit_run reads all six back in enqueue parameter order (0x004306f5-0x0043076e); llm_tact_unit_owner_tick (0x00433641/0x00433658) and enqueue itself (0x0042b400/0x0042b416) pair the flag with the op of the SAME slot; and llm_tact_render_view's debug overlay prints both for the same slot under the shipped format string at 0x00500338, "%2d. nr.com:%2d com:%2d who:%1d" -- the developers' own name for the byte is `who`. THE FAR-END OBJECTION DISSOLVES: +0x5d4 is not a leftover hole but a real written byte, and +0x5d4..+0x5de and +0x5df..+0x5e9 are two MORE records of the identical shape (the immediate ATTACK/AIM and FACE/TURN slots the enqueue writes on its op==2 and op==6 short-circuits), the third of which ends exactly where move_aborted_op begins at +0x5ea. Three records tile with zero orphan bytes; the old model left two demonstrably-written bytes unexplained. APPLIED: new type /llm/llm_tact_unit_cmd_entry (0xb bytes, all six fields commented) and tact_unit_record+0x54 retyped llm_tact_unit_cmd_entry[128], absorbing the old cmd_slot_flag + five 'ENTRY-0 ALIAS' scalars; field_5d5 renamed attack_cmd_op. Record size unchanged at 0x5f4. Scope (a) deliberately: the two immediate records were NOT retyped, because that would fold the hand-named, separately documented aim_x/aim_y into arg2/arg3. todo:struct discharged on both enqueue and resubmit. NO src/mh_dll RIPPLE -- tact_unit_record is not in the generated struct header and no hand-written source names it. TWO RESIDUE FINDINGS CONFIRMED FROM THE DISASSEMBLY, not inherited: op 0x46 CLEAR zeroes 127 entries and skips the head (the loop at 0x0042b5f5-0x0042b642 runs its counter 0..0x7e and increments the slot index BEFORE each store), correcting the enqueue plate's 'wipes all 128'; and interrupt_flag is never cleared on dequeue, so it is stale whenever op == 0 -- benign today, but a reimplementation that zero-fills the whole entry would diverge on a byte-compare. Both are now in the field comments and the plate.

findings.symbol: the committed clobberer manifests are STALE against the fixed classifier, and 9 functions are already in DB-vs-manifest drift
findings.why_not_blocking: Nothing reads these manifests automatically -- set_calling_convention.py takes an explicit request file a human builds -- and the direction of the old error was the safe one (a false clobberer costs an honest extraout_ artifact, never a silently stale value).
findings.current: classify_reg_preservation.py's PUSHAD/POPAD blindness was fixed 2026-08-24, but the manifests it fed were NOT regenerated and no calling convention was re-pinned. Measured before/after over the whole binary in one ReVA session: ECX clobbers 265 -> 219, EBX 487 -> 439, EDX 1169 -> 1126 (saved +39/+36/+27, never_writes +7/+12/+16). So ~46 rows per register in each committed manifest are now known-false.
findings.proposed: A dedicated session: regenerate the manifests from the fixed classifier, then re-pin conventions with README sections 3-4's validation discipline -- gate green, dll_call_protos ok count unchanged, and a site-level read of the largest mover. Not a drive-by.
findings.evidence: 40 functions in /eng/mh.exe open with PUSHAD and all 40 contain POPAD, so all 40 preserve every GP register by construction; all 40 appeared in BOTH manifests (a 100% false-positive rate on this shape). NINE OF THEM NOW CARRY __watcall IN THE DB while the manifests still pin them volatile -- 0x00436f30 llm_tact_fov_raycast_stencil, 0x0043ac65 llm_tact_tlo_tile_blit, 0x0043c0e1/0043c155/0043c1dd/0043c266 llm_tact_view_shift_*, 0x0043c3dc llm_tact_tile_overlay_refresh, 0x004a17b3 llm_strat_minimap_render, 0x004a5167 llm_strat_render_ground_tile -- so a classify + set_calling_convention run made from the stale manifests would move all nine BACK onto __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile and re-introduce artifacts that sessions cleared by hand at EN v339/v341.
findings.resolution:
RE-DERIVED AND HALF-APPLIED; what remains is named below. Re-ran the fixed classifier over the whole binary and reproduced the finding's own numbers independently: ECX clobbers 219, EBX 439, EDX 1126. Then built the missing tool -- tools/gen_reg_clobberers.py, with a --check drift gate (mutation-tested: dropping one row exits 1, restoring is green) -- and regenerated both manifests. Measured delta lands where the finding predicted (~46/register): ECX 272 -> 229 (-45/+2), EBX 493 -> 453 (-47/+7), the EBX split moving 252 -> 207 both-registers and 241 -> 246 EBX-only. ALL NINE trap functions the finding named are gone from both manifests, so the committed data is no longer known-false and a future classify + set_calling_convention pass can no longer move them back onto __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile. REMAINING, one step: run mh_set_calling_convention.py to re-pin the conventions the refreshed manifests now describe, with tools/ghidra/README.md sections 3-4's validation discipline -- gate green, dll_call_protos `ok` count unchanged, and a site-level read of the largest mover. The finding itself says that is not a drive-by and I agree; no convention was re-pinned here. Two related defects found and fixed on the way: see 2026-08-24-1348-2.

STILL DEFERRED after 2026-08-29's drain, DELIBERATELY -- but the remaining step is no longer an unscoped 'dedicated session'. It is now MEASURED, so the next session decides rather than digs. Confirmed first that the regenerated data has not rotted: `python tools/gen_reg_clobberers.py --check` says CURRENT (ECX 229, EBX 246 + 207). THE DELTA IS 46 EBX ROWS AND 26 ECX ROWS, not hundreds. Comparing every manifest row against the convention actually pinned in the DB at EN v370: of the EBX manifest's 453 rows, 407 already agree (223 on __mh_watcall_ebx_volatile, 184 on __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile) and exactly 46 disagree -- 23 pinned __watcall that the manifest wants on __mh_watcall_ebx_volatile (llm_ui_bldg_worker_adjust_apply, llm_tact_unit_get_muzzle_offset, llm_strat_bldg_get_coords, llm_strat_unit_get_coords, map_unit_PutOnMap, llm_strat_storage_can_exit, ...) and 23 pinned __watcall that it wants on __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile (llm_strat_pathfind_build_steps, llm_tact_move_find_approach_tile, llm_strat_weapon_pixel_distance_ratio, llm_bldg_queue_construction, llm_strat_projectile_spawn, llm_strat_turret_acquire_target, ...). Of the ECX manifest's 229 rows, 186 are on __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile and 17 on __mh_watcall_ecx_volatile, leaving 26 on plain __watcall. Reproduce by resolving each manifest row's addr through getFunctionAt().getCallingConventionName(). NOTE THE DIRECTION HAS FLIPPED, and this is the reason it is worth a session rather than being dropped. The original finding's comfort was that a stale manifest errs safely (a false clobberer costs an honest extraout_ artifact, never a silently stale value). These 72 are the OPPOSITE: the DB pins __watcall, which declares EBX/ECX <unaffected>, on functions the fixed classifier says clobber them -- so a caller's decompile currently assumes a register survives a call that kills it. That is the unsafe direction. Caveat before anyone treats all 72 as defects: the classifier's `unsure` bucket (pushed, no exit path proven to restore) is folded into `clobbers` conservatively, so some fraction of the 72 are unproven and re-pinning those costs only an artifact. Split the worklist on `why` before pinning. WHY THIS SESSION DID NOT APPLY IT, stated as a judgement rather than a shrug: it is a ripple I would risk leaving half-applied, and a half-applied convention pass is worse than none. One mitigating measurement in its favour for whoever takes it -- the three models differ only in `killedbycall`, not in parameter storage, so dll_call_protos' marshalling shapes and mh_calls.gen.h should NOT move; the ripple is decompiler register-liveness, which is why README sections 3-4 ask for the `ok`-count-unchanged check and a site-level read of the largest mover rather than a rig run. Applying it is tools/set_calling_convention.py, which takes a hand-built {convention, functions[]} request -- so it is two requests, one per target model, plus a third for the ECX-only set.

findings.symbol: the shim set is derived from `currentProgram`, so a Ghidra-side tool that uses getCurrentProgram() gets no shim and is unrunnable through ReVA
findings.why_not_blocking: Worked around by exec'ing the repo file from an inline run-script with getCurrentProgram/monitor injected. Costs nothing but the workaround.
findings.current: install_ghidra_shims.py decides a tool needs a shim iff it names `currentProgram`. tools/classify_reg_preservation.py is a Ghidra script -- @category mh, uses monitor and the FlatProgramAPI -- but calls getCurrentProgram() instead, so it is absent from the derived set. `--check` reports 36 ok / 0 missing while a real Ghidra-side tool has no shim at all.
findings.proposed: Widen the predicate to `currentProgram` OR `getCurrentProgram` OR `getState()` -- and add a marker test so the negative case is pinned, the way the file's own docstring argues the derived set should behave.
findings.evidence: `run-script {scriptPath: tools/classify_reg_preservation.py}` is refused ('outside registered script directories'); `install_ghidra_shims.py --list | grep classify` is empty; `--check` says 36 ok, 0 missing. This is the exact failure the installer was written to prevent (mh_gen_codemap.py, 2026-08-22): a Ghidra-side tool whose only symptom is 'Script not found'.
findings.resolution: APPLIED, and it was two defects stacked, not one. (1) The predicate is widened to accept `currentProgram` OR `getCurrentProgram` OR `getState()` -- exactly as the finding proposed -- and a new --selftest pins all three PLUS the two negative cases, so a future narrowing fails in the tool instead of silently on the next new script. The derived set goes 36 -> 37 and mh_classify_reg_preservation.py is installed. (2) Installing it exposed the next layer, which the finding could not have seen: classify_reg_preservation derived REPO from __file__, which under the shim is the SHIM's path (the shim is `exec(open(<repo>/tools/<n>.py).read())`), so it tried to write C:\Users\user\tmp\reg_preservation.json and died with FileNotFoundError AFTER 26 seconds of classification. It now uses the same program-derived repo_root() every other Ghidra-side tool here uses. Verified end to end: the classifier runs through the shim and writes to the repo.

findings.symbol: the bar-sprite hit-test mechanism is half-derived: one cell with no referrers, one with no writer, and the decoder is unnamed
findings.why_not_blocking: None of the three is read by a migration domain, and the two named cells carry plates stating exactly what is and is not settled.
findings.current: 0x00824fb0 has ZERO references binary-wide, so its role cannot be derived by the referrer-set method and its misleading minimap name was deleted rather than replaced. _G_LLM_GFX_SPRITE_HITTEST_CURSOR (0x00824fb8) and its comparison target DAT_00825094 have no traceable WRITER, so what sets the cursor is unknown. FUN_004a763f -- the RLE decoder/blitter that reads them and sets _G_LLM_HITTEST_HIT -- is still unnamed.
findings.proposed: Name FUN_004a763f first: it is the one with a body to read, it is a reusable sprite primitive rather than a bar-specific one, and naming it probably settles the other three. For 0x00824fb0 specifically, a computed/indexed-access sweep (scan_raw_pointers.py) is the only instrument left -- a reference through a register-held base is invisible to the reference manager.
findings.evidence: find-cross-references returns 0 in both directions for 0x00824fb0. FUN_004a763f reads 0x00824fb8 at 0x004a76aa at the 0xFF stream terminator and compares it against DAT_00825094; it walks the same RLE dialect llm_gfx_build_bar_sprite_rle emits (0xFF terminator, 0xFE row marker, 0x20/0x40/0x60/0x80/0xa0/0xc0 skip opcodes) and advances a destination cursor scaled by _G_LLM_FB_PITCH.
findings.resolution:
MECHANISM SETTLED, AND THE FINDING'S PREMISE WAS WRONG; only the mechanical apply remains, deferred at the context-budget stop of session 2026-08-24-1636. The finding assumed FUN_004a763f is 'a reusable sprite primitive' whose naming would settle the other three cells. It is not reusable -- IT IS DEAD, and that inverts what the three cells mean.
WHAT IT IS: a hit-test-only walk, not a blit. Over its 142 bytes (0x004a763f-0x004a76cc) it decodes the same RLE dialect as llm_gfx_blit_sprite_rle (0xFF end, 0xFE row, 0x20/0x40/0x60/0x80/0xa0/0xc0 skips) and NEVER writes a pixel -- only ADD ESI (source skip) and framebuffer-pitch cursor bookkeeping. At the 0xFF terminator it DISCARDS that cursor and instead does MOV EDI,[0x00824fb8] / MOV AX,[0x00825094] / CMP word [EDI],AX, setting _G_LLM_HITTEST_HIT. It is a near-exact structural twin of the LIVE llm_gfx_sprite_rle_row_skip (0x004a665a, 16 callers), which differs only in taking the UI-surface path and delegating to llm_gfx_hittest_check instead of doing its own embedded compare -- i.e. it is the framebuffer-path counterpart that PREDATES the shared llm_gfx_hittest_begin/_check/_check_blit design the main blitter uses today.
DEAD, by four independent instruments, which is the bar docs/dead-ends.md sets for this claim (a byte scan alone is vacuous for CALL rel32; the reference manager alone is vacuous for computed calls; the combination is what settles it): reference manager 0 incoming; call_graph_no_crt.json tail_jumps 0 entries as source or target; whole-image byte scan for its own LE address 0 hits, with the scan VALIDATED against a control (_G_LLM_FB_PITCH's address returned 73 hits across 36 functions, proving the scan traverses the whole image); search-decompilation for '4a763f' 1 hit, its own signature. Plus a structural argument: it has NO PUSHAD despite ending POPAD;RET on both exits, so it is only valid entered on a caller's PUSHAD frame -- and no such caller exists.
THAT SETTLES THE OTHER THREE CELLS by making them consistent rather than mysterious. _G_LLM_GFX_SPRITE_HITTEST_CURSOR (0x00824fb8) and DAT_00825094 have exactly ONE occurrence image-wide each -- the two reads inside this dead function -- so 'no traceable writer' is not a gap in the search, it is the fact: nothing writes them because nothing runs. Both are .bss, so a live dereference would null-deref, which is itself evidence the path never executes. Neither is a folded-bias alias of the neighbouring _G_LLM_TACT_FOV_STENCIL (0x0082509c): the deltas are 0xE4 and 0x08, and no other instruction anywhere encodes either disp32, so there is no stencil-indexing access to fold against.
0x00824fb0 STAYS UNNAMED and the finding's own instrument (scan_raw_pointers / a computed-access sweep) is exhausted: zero occurrences of its address anywhere in the image, so xref, tail-jump, byte scan and text search are all spent. Only a runtime write-breakpoint could settle it. It sits adjacent to the other two members of the same abandoned triad, which is the most likely reading but is not evidence.
REMAINING, three mechanical steps: (1) rename FUN_004a763f -> llm_gfx_sprite_rle_row_skip_hittest with a plate carrying the UNREACHABLE evidence above; (2) commit `void __watcall(void)` on it, which also clears its unaff_ESI / in_stack_00000018 / in_stack_00000020 / CONCAT44 fake-return artifacts; (3) OPTIONALLY rename DAT_00825094 -> _G_LLM_GFX_SPRITE_HITTEST_SAVED_PIXEL_LEGACY -- a 16-bit sentinel/expected-pixel value, LEAD-grade, inferred structurally from the live _G_LLM_HITTEST_SAVED_PIXEL (0x005d8850) rather than from any writer of its own. Do (3) only if you accept a name derived by analogy; leaving it DAT_ is also defensible for a dead cell.

CLOSED 2026-08-29 at EN v370, with step (2) DECLINED on evidence and step (3) replaced by something better. RE-DERIVED FIRST -- the deferral's dead claim holds, but one of its four instruments was reported with the wrong control and is re-stated here: (1) reference manager: 7 incoming refs, ALL this body's own internal UNCONDITIONAL_JUMPs (0x004a7667/6f/79/83/8b/91/a6), zero external; CONTROL = the live twin llm_gfx_sprite_rle_row_skip @0x004a665a shows 16. (2) whole-image byte scan for its own LE address over all 2892288 initialized bytes: 0 hits, so no fn-pointer table holds it -- but the DEFERRAL'S CONTROL FOR THIS WAS _G_LLM_FB_PITCH, a DATA address, which proves the scan traverses without proving it can see a function reference; the honest control is a function address, and a function referenced only by CALL rel32 returns 0 hits too, so this instrument speaks ONLY to fn-ptr tables and instrument (1) is what covers direct calls. (My first attempt at this scan returned 0 for the positive control as well -- the buffer was never populated -- so it was vacuous; caught by the control, re-run correctly, positive control then returns 3 hits.) (3) call_graph_no_crt.json: 0 links in or out, absent from the 120-entry tail_jumps ledger. (4) search-decompilation: 1 hit, its own signature. Plus the structural argument, verified in the listing: no PUSHAD at entry, both terminator exits POPAD;RET (@0x004a76c2/@0x004a76cb), so it is only valid on a caller's PUSHAD frame -- and 0x004a7600-0x004a763e is not even disassembled, so nothing falls through into it either. STEP (1) DONE: renamed FUN_004a763f -> llm_gfx_sprite_rle_row_skip_hittest with a plate carrying all of the above plus what it actually does (decodes the shared RLE dialect, writes NO pixel, advances a cursor by _G_LLM_FB_PITCH, and at the 0xFF terminator discards it to do its own embedded compare into _G_LLM_HITTEST_HIT @0x005204e1). STEP (2) DECLINED, and this is the substantive departure. Committing `void __watcall(void)` would clear the unaff_ESI / in_stack_ / CONCAT44 artifacts by ASSERTING 'no inputs' about a body whose inputs are ambient: ESI is the RLE source pointer and EDI the destination cursor, neither a __watcall argument register -- the same un-prototypable shape ai_ready_ack.json already records for llm_strat_ai_engage_sort_candidates_by_dist. The stack discipline is not uniform either: the 0xFE row-marker arm exits with a BARE RET @0x004a765a while the terminator arms POPAD first, and the 0xFF arm does `POP EAX` @0x004a7647 before jumping to the compare -- two exits serving two different frames. On dead code the artifacts cost nothing; a false prototype would cost a reader. Recorded in the plate instead. STEP (3) REPLACED: rather than naming DAT_00825094 by analogy with _G_LLM_HITTEST_SAVED_PIXEL, both it and _G_LLM_GFX_SPRITE_HITTEST_CURSOR (0x00824fb8) got EOL comments carrying the evidence -- that their sole occurrence image-wide is inside this dead body, that 'no traceable writer' is the fact rather than a search gap, that they are .bss so a live dereference would fault, and that neither is a folded alias of _G_LLM_TACT_FOV_STENCIL. The evidence is preserved where a reader finds it without a name asserting a reading nothing writes. 0x00824fb0 stays unnamed as the deferral said.

findings.symbol: the cfg SYSTEM parser does not bounds-check `PLANET <n>` -- n >= 32 overwrites the INVENTION scratch
findings.why_not_blocking: Retail cfgs stay in range; this is a modding/robustness note, not a defect in the recovered model.
findings.current: The SYSTEM section's PLANET handler parses %d and does `SHL EAX,0x7`, writing the name into 0xe5a710 + n*0x80 with no clamp. The scratch template holds 32 planet slots followed by INVENTION at 0xe5b710 and ICON at 0xe5b790, so `PLANET 32` in a cfg would land on the INVENTION scratch. Only the COPY loop into the final record is bounded (k < 0x20).
findings.proposed: Record it in whichever doc covers cfg parsing before anyone ships a mod that edits SYSTEM sections; if the patcher ever validates cfg input, this is a cheap guard.
findings.evidence: Parser body 0x004afe2b-0x004aff6e; the SHL at 0x004afec0; cfg_CopyStaticToDynamic 0x004ac8dc commits PLANET k to TEXT[n]+0x180+k*0x80 for k = 0..0x1f, and 0x180 + 32*0x80 = 0x1180 = the cfg record stride, which closes the arithmetic and shows the 32 is a template bound rather than a checked one.
findings.resolution: APPLIED as the finding proposed -- recorded in docs/cfg-strategic.md, in the INIT.CFG keyword grammar section next to the SYSTEM/PLANET rows, with the full arithmetic: the SHL EAX,0x7 at 0x004afec0 writing 0xe5a710 + n*0x80 with no clamp; the scratch template's 32 planet slots followed by INVENTION at 0xe5b710 and ICON at 0xe5b790; and cfg_CopyStaticToDynamic (0x004ac8dc) committing k = 0..0x1f to TEXT[n]+0x180+k*0x80, where 0x180 + 32*0x80 = 0x1180 = the cfg record stride, which is what shows the 32 is a template bound rather than a checked one. Kept the finding's own framing that this is a modding/robustness note rather than a defect in the recovered model, and left the 'cheap guard if the patcher ever validates cfg input' as the actionable half.

findings.addr: 0x00583416 llm_strat_pathfind_flood_search_driver; plus 7 PUSHAD functions with ret=undefined
findings.symbol: the PUSHAD cohort has two arity/return leftovers the v339 spill test never re-derived
findings.why_not_blocking: No migration domain is blocked on any of them today; migration_ready is green over readers, ai and sim.
findings.current: llm_strat_pathfind_flood_search_driver carries params=1 on a PUSHAD prologue. That is not automatically wrong -- PUSHAD does not preclude a register parameter, it only makes one uninferable -- but it is the single member of the 40-function PUSHAD set whose arity was never put through the spill test that corrected llm_strat_minimap_render. Separately, 7 of the 40 still carry ret=undefined (0x0043abfe, 0x0043b241, 0x0043c323, 0x004a5d3b, 0x0055bd7f, 0x0055e1cc, plus unnamed 0x0058013c/0x00580e29/0x0066ee56) although a POPAD;RET exit makes `void` provable by the same save-area argument used at 0x004a17b3.
findings.proposed: Run the spill test on the driver (a real register parameter in this build is spilled to a frame local right after SUB ESP,n; a PUSHAD prologue has no frame to spill into), and settle the 7 returns by checking each for a store into the PUSHAD save area before its POPAD.
findings.evidence: Enumerated during finding 2026-08-24-0029-8's re-derivation: 40 functions open with PUSHAD and all 40 contain POPAD. The method that settled 0x004a17b3 -- read-before-write over all 7 GP registers, plus a scan for any store into the save area -- applies unchanged.
findings.resolution: APPLIED at EN v363, and the re-derivation found ONE MORE THING the deferred note did not contain. RE-DERIVED FIRST, two independent legs over all seven bodies, using Listing.getInstructions (NOT get-decompilation's assembly field -- the note's own tool-defect (a) says that field drops PUSHAD/POPAD, and I did not want to inherit the artefact I was checking for). Leg 1: every one opens with PUSHAD at its entry instruction, POPAD count equals RET count, and a sweep of every instruction in each Function.getBody() found ZERO stores with an ESP- or EBP-relative destination. Leg 2, stronger and not in the note: POPAD is the instruction IMMEDIATELY preceding EVERY RET in all seven (9 exits across the set), and every RET is a plain RET with no imm -- so POPAD reloads EAX from the untouched entry save area on every path and the function cannot return anything. COMMITTED ret=void for all seven (0x0043b241, 0x004a5d3b, 0x0055bd7f, 0x0055e1cc, 0x0058013c, 0x0066ee56, 0x00580e29) via commit_prototypes OVERRIDE, preserving each one's existing __mh_watcall_ecx_ebx_volatile. THE EXTRA FINDING: the void commit made three of them report HARD:in_EAX, which they did NOT carry before (proto_artifacts.json, regenerated minutes earlier, has no row for any of the three). That is not a regression from the commit -- it is the commit REVEALING a real missing parameter that ret=undefined had been masking. Read-before-write on EAX confirms it at the SECOND instruction of each, immediately after PUSHAD and before any write to EAX: 0x0055bd80 MOV BL,[EAX+0x16]; 0x0055e1dd MOV [EAX+0x1c],0x0; 0x00580e2a MOV BL,[EAX+0x16]. That is the identical shape to 0x00583416, which the DB already carries as void (void *ctx) storage EAX:4 -- and which is exactly the shared pathfind request/route record the note's own STRUCT LEAD describes (+0x16/+0x17/+0x18/+0x1c). Committed params=[void *ctx] storage EAX:4 on those three, mirroring 0x00583416; all three then verify clean. The other four take no EAX and were left at zero params. CONFIRMED, NO ACTION, as the note said: 0x00583416's params=1 is correct and was not touched. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE -- the CONVENTION. findings.symbol: two production-queue leads: an unreconciled 0x32 vs 0xff cap, and an unnamed-parameter prototype
findings.why_not_blocking: Both are inside an already-named, already-prototyped cluster; neither blocks a readiness check.
findings.current: (a) llm_ui_bldg_units_panel_row_count_update bounds its stepping by `target_count`, and both callers pass 0xff -- effectively uncapped at that layer -- while llm_strat_bldg_order_production_add clamps the running total to 0x32 in its own body (0x004685ee-0x00468628). Two caps in play and nobody has read production_add's body to reconcile them. (b) llm_strat_bldg_prod_get_queued_count is `int f(ushort param_1, int param_2, int a2)` -- unnamed params, and `ushort` for what the call sites treat as a plain player index.
findings.proposed: (a) Read production_add's body and state which cap actually binds, in its plate. (b) By analogy with production_add/_remove's own parameters the names are almost certainly player_idx / bldg_idx / unit_type, and the first is probably int -- but that is an analogy, so derive it from the body before committing.
findings.evidence: Call sites pass llm_strat_bldg_prod_get_queued_count(PlayerSide, (uint)_G_LLM_STRAT_UI_SELECTED_BLDG_INDEX, a2) -- the identical argument pattern to production_add/_remove. The 0xff comes from the two button handlers at 0x004129a8 / 0x004129e3.
findings.resolution: APPLIED, and the re-derivation OVERTURNED the finding's own location claim. (a) The 0x32 clamp is NOT in llm_strat_bldg_order_production_add's body. That function is 0x0046dae0-0x0046db57 and does nothing but set args[0]=unit_type, args[1]=1 and enqueue. The clamp lives ~31 KB away in llm_strat_order_queue_dispatch (entry 0x00466892), bldg-lane case 3 for order 0x6d, and it fires LATER, when the queue drains: CMP EAX,0x32 at 0x004685ee on (args[1] + queued_count[0]), then SUB / MOV [.. + 0xbb4ee4],EDX at 0x0046861e-0x00468628 REWRITING the queued order's own args[1] down to the remaining headroom before applying it to BOTH queued_count[0] and queued_count[unit_type] -- so 0x32 bounds the AGGREGATE and no per-type slot can exceed it either. Verified the containment independently: getFunctionContaining(0x004685ee) returns llm_strat_order_queue_dispatch. The UI's 0xff is real but inert; it could only matter if the ceiling were raised above 255. The defective text was the PLATE on llm_ui_bldg_units_panel_row_count_update (0x004127ef), which said 'production_add clamps the running total to 0x32 in its own body' -- corrected in place, with production_add's own plate (which was right all along) named as the reference. (b) Prototype committed: `int __watcall llm_strat_bldg_prod_get_queued_count(ushort player_idx, int bldg_idx, int unit_type)` at AX:2 / EDX:4 / EBX:4. The names are NOT the finding's analogy: player_idx is read via MOVZX word at four separate sites (so ushort/AX:2 is the real width, confirmed against the live storage), bldg_idx indexes buildings[player][bldg].sub_id, and unit_type indexes productions[player][sub_id].queued_count[] directly -- and both call sites pass the SAME local into this function and into production_add's independently-corroborated unit_type parameter, which is shared-variable identity rather than analogy.

findings.symbol: a `movs` count is a PROVENANCE, not a direction -- every rep-movs SOURCE was claimed as a WRITE

findings.why_not_blocking: Nothing reads it, so no reading rests on the name; it is registered and plated, and R8 is green.
findings.current: Named _G_LLM_TACT_UNIT_ACTIVE_COUNT, i.e. a count of live tactical units.
findings.proposed: No single name fits the evidence, which is why this is open rather than applied. A plate recording the contradiction is already on the symbol; the decision needed is whether to rename it for what the spawn path stores (a slot index), leave it, or delete the name.
findings.evidence: llm_tact_unit_spawn stores at 0x0042bb1a the value in [EBP-0x20] -- the FREE-SLOT INDEX returned by the scan at 0x0042b9a8 (`CMP byte [EAX+0x8260d0],1 / JNC` over the roster), the same local every `IMUL ...,0x5f4` in that function uses to address _G_LLM_TACT_UNITS. llm_tact_unit_destroy (0x00432014) and llm_tact_unit_despawn (0x004320ed) DEC it. A last-spawned SLOT INDEX and a DEC on an arbitrary removal are not consistent with each other under first-free allocation. It does not matter today: the 4-byte address occurs exactly THREE times image-wide (Memory.findBytes) and all three are those writes, so NOTHING reads it. Beware the confusable sibling _G_LLM_TACT_ACTIVE_UNIT_COUNT at 0x005590ec, which IS a real recomputed tally (reset+INC in llm_tact_squad_roster_refresh and llm_tact_active_unit_count_hud_draw, read as the mission-end predicate by llm_tact_frame at 0x00429c36).
findings.resolution: RE-DERIVED AND CONFIRMED, then DECIDED: keep the name, correct the plate. Every mechanical claim in the finding holds. I re-read the spawn scan (0x0042b98e-0x0042b9c0 walks slots 1..0x80 for the first with byte[idx*0x5f4 + 0x8260d0] == 0), confirmed the store at 0x0042bb1a assigns that [EBP-0x20] index, and confirmed the two DECs at 0x00432014 / 0x004320ed each follow a clear of the same occupancy byte. The 'nothing reads it' negative was re-run by a second, independent method -- a whole-image sweep of all 252238 instructions for the LE dword, per docs/dead-ends.md sect. A -- returning the same three sites, all writes, and 7 sites for the confusable sibling _G_LLM_TACT_ACTIVE_UNIT_COUNT at 0x005590ec. ONE THING THE FINDING DID NOT HAVE, and it is what decided the call: the two readings are not simply irreconcilable. Under first-free allocation a gap-free roster puts the newest unit at slot N, so 'slot just filled' and 'live population' COINCIDE, and the DEC keeps them coinciding when the unit removed is the last; the name only becomes wrong on the first spawn that refills a hole. So ACTIVE_COUNT records the intent and is exact in the common case, whereas a mechanism-derived LAST_SPAWN_SLOT would be equally wrong at both DEC sites -- while costing a rename across mh_addrs.gen.h, the RID_ constant in mh_regions.gen.h, mh_shadow.gen.h, four tact TU banners and the shadow/region manifests, for a global with no reader at all. Rewrote the plate to carry the mechanism, that condition, the two derivations and the sibling warning. Nothing renamed, nothing deleted. EN v359.

findings.symbol: llm_tact_unit_move_advance DECs a byte inside the STRATEGIC path-waypoint buffer and an earlier plate calls it a per-tile visibility refcount
findings.why_not_blocking: The address resolves inside a NAMED region, so R4/R9 are green and no tactical readiness check fires on it. It is a semantic question, not a markup gap.
findings.current: 0x00aee8c0 is typed llm_strat_path_waypoint[240000] (_G_LLM_STRAT_PATH_BUFFERS). llm_tact_unit_move_advance's plate describes the byte one past it as 'the per-tile visibility counter at DAT_00aee8c1'.
findings.proposed: Settle which reading is right. Either (a) it is a folded-bias alias of a DIFFERENT array -- the family confirmed three times on 2026-08-24, see docs/dead-ends.md -- and the plate's 'visibility refcount' is correct while the containing type is coincidence; or (b) the path buffer's declared extent is wrong and the two objects overlap; or (c) tactical genuinely reuses the strategic path buffer as scratch, which would be a real aliasing fact a reimplementation must preserve. Derive EAX's scale at 0x00431067 to decide: a tile-index scale points at (a) or (c), a waypoint-slot scale at the path buffer.
findings.evidence: llm_tact_unit_move_advance 0x00431067 `DEC byte ptr [EAX + 0xaee8c1]` and 0x0043109c `CMP byte ptr [EAX + 0xaee8c1],0x0`. The declared array is 240000 x 2 B = 480000 B, consistent with the 0x258-per-slot stride the tact_unit_record.move_path_step comment documents, so the extent is not obviously wrong -- which is what makes the overlap worth checking rather than assuming.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-24 (TACT-WRITERS) by the scale test this finding itself named. At 0x00431067 `DEC byte ptr [EAX + 0xaee8c1]`, EAX = owner*0xea60 + slot*0x258 + step*2 (0x00431046 IMUL EAX,EAX,0x258; 0x0043104c IMUL EDX,[EBP-0x10],0xea60; 0x00431063 ADD EAX,EAX) -- a WAYPOINT-SLOT scale, which by this finding's own criterion points at the path buffer. So hypothesis (a) folded-bias alias of a different array is out, (b) wrong extent is out, and (c) is right but narrower than feared: the +1 is the run_length FIELD OFFSET inside the 2-byte {heading, run_length} waypoint, folded into the disp32 the way Watcom folds base+field everywhere here. The address is _G_LLM_STRAT_PATH_BUFFERS[owner][slot][step].run_length; 0x0043109c CMPs the same byte to decide whether to advance move_path_step. The 'per-tile visibility refcount' reading was simply wrong -- it predates the region being typed -- and llm_tact_unit_move_advance's plate has been rewritten (EN v349), dropping the stale todo:globals. The sibling plate on llm_tact_move_path_preview_walk ('DAT_00aee8c1 is the odd/repeat bytes of _G_LLM_STRAT_PATH_BUFFERS'), tasks/map-naming.md and src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/sim_path_group_steps.h all already said the correct thing; only this one plate disagreed.

findings.symbol: the tactical planet round-trip is called unconditionally but its EFFECT is conditional on file I/O, and both failure paths are silent
findings.why_not_blocking: It is an ORIGINAL-GAME defect, not a markup gap and not a reimplementation bug. Nothing in the readiness predicate or the ownership interlock fires on it. It is recorded because TACT-WRITERS' exception is scoped to the case where the I/O succeeds, and a later reader must not re-derive the word 'unconditionally' from the earlier prose.
findings.current: docs/tactical-probe.md Sect. 5 and TACT-WRITERS' original premise both say the shared planes are restored by an UNCONDITIONAL disk round-trip and therefore 'nothing tactical writes into those planes can outlive the excursion'. The two CALLS are indeed unconditional; the two EFFECTS are not.
findings.proposed: Decide, in TACT1, whether to PRESERVE this behaviour (it is what the original does, and a reimplementation must match it bit-for-bit under the oracle) or to guard it in the hosted build the way the DLL's --tactical verb now does. Record the choice; do not leave it implicit.
findings.evidence: ENTRY: 0x0044d38f CALL map_SavePlanetToDisk, 0x0044d394 MOV byte[0x005202d0],0x6 -- no TEST/Jcc between them, so the return is discarded. map_SavePlanetToDisk returns 0 without writing when utils_open_file fails and 0 when any block write fails; that file is the ONLY backup of the planet the mission is about to wipe. EXIT: 0x0044d41d TEST EAX,EAX / 0x0044d41f JNZ -- the false arm only skips the four finalizers and sets the function's own return to 0, and both llm_tact_frame call sites (0x00429c87, 0x00429df3) are a CALL followed immediately by JMP to the epilogue, so that return is discarded too. _G_LLM_GAME_MODE is already 2 (0x0044d3e4, before the reload) and the planet is already latched VISITED (0x0044d404), so a failed reload resumes strategic mode on a planet still holding tactical's 128x128 wipe, and SwitchToPlanet (0x0044cf53) will later LOAD it rather than regenerate. A mid-way block failure restores the planes PARTIALLY and still returns 0. Plates on both functions record this (EN v349).
findings.resolution: RE-DERIVED AND CLOSED: the decision the finding asked for is settled, and settled by a rule the user has already recorded rather than by this session inventing one. Law 2 (bit-identical behaviour outranks correctness; preserve original bugs) requires the reimplementation to reproduce 'called unconditionally, effect conditional on I/O, failure silent' literally -- and the shipped translation already does: src/mh_dll/libmh/tact/tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic.h step 4 documents rc == 0 skipping the finalizers with the local success flag left 0 and discarded by every caller, and TACT1A closed that row `verified`. The doc half is already corrected too -- docs/tactical-probe.md Sect. 5 carries a CORRECTED 2026-08-24 block replacing the word 'unconditional', and plates on both functions record it (EN v349). What was genuinely missing was the finding's own requirement, 'record the choice; do not leave it implicit': the decision lived only in prose no tool reads. FIXED AT THE SOURCE rather than in prose -- added a `preserve_bugs` block to tools/data/migration/tact.json keyed on llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic, which gen_migration.py propagates into the manifest's per-function `preserve_bug` field, which migration_session.py --start flags and the translator brief reads. Verified it propagates. NOT recorded for the entry-side mirror in llm_strat_try_enter_tactical_mission (0x0044d38f, the discarded map_SavePlanetToDisk return): that function is in no migration manifest, so a key for it would be inert and would rot -- its half is carried in this resolution, in its Ghidra plate and in the tactical-probe correction block instead. Whether the HOSTED build should guard the round-trip the way the DLL's --tactical verb does is a product question outside the migration and is stated as such in the preserve_bugs entry.

findings.current: travel_dx was documented only as 'accumulated X displacement since spawn (+= vel_x per step); sqrt(travel_dx^2+travel_dy^2) checked vs fx_type.range_max. Init 0' -- accurate for its own writer/reader (llm_tact_fx_update_projectile) but silent about a SECOND, incompatible reader.
findings.proposed: Document that llm_tact_tile_rebuild_occupancy_layer (0x00433dfc, 0x00433e41-0x00433e4c) reads this field's first three raw bytes (+0x12/+0x13/+0x14) as (col,row,stamp) for every active FX-pool entry owned by the reload map, and that this is NOT a designed encoding: llm_tact_fx_spawn (0x0042bdce, lines 37-40) zeroes travel_dx/travel_dy for EVERY fx_type at spawn, and llm_tact_fx_update_projectile only ever advances travel_dx inside its fx_type<0x20 arm (gated 0x004316b7) -- so for a fx_type>=0x20 'pure animation effect' these three bytes are provably (0,0,0) for the entry's whole life, and for a moving projectile they are the low mantissa bytes of an accumulated double, not a col/row/stamp triple. A prior session's progress note (tracker/reimpl.yaml, TACT1A) had characterized this as '(col, row, occupancy-stamp)' without checking the writers; that characterization is not wrong about WHAT is read but is unsupported as a claim about WHY -- a future reader could mistake it for deliberate design.

findings.current: Ghidra types 0x00500452 as a 10-byte string "MINE   " (get-data: dataType string, length 10, hexBytes 4d494e45202020000000).
findings.proposed: The declared 10-byte length oversteps by 2 bytes into a SEPARATE, real double constant at 0x0050045a (180.0 exactly, confirmed via ReVA read-memory: 00 00 00 00 00 80 66 40 LE) that llm_tact_calc_dir24 (0x0042e156, FMUL double ptr [EDX+0x0050045a]) reads as its own datum. The string is likely 8 bytes ("MINE\0\0\0\0") with the double beginning immediately after at +8; the current 10-byte string declaration should be shortened (or the double explicitly typed at 0x0050045a) so the two data items stop overlapping in the DB.
findings.evidence: get-data(/eng/mh.exe, 0x00500452) -> string, length 10, hexBytes 4d494e45202020000000 (M I N E sp sp sp 00 00 00). read-memory(/eng/mh.exe, 0x0050045a, 8) -> 00 00 00 00 00 80 66 40 (LE double = 180.0 exactly, struct.pack('<d',180.0).hex()=='0000000000806640', confirmed bit-identical). 0x0050045a - 0x00500452 = 0x8, i.e. the double starts 2 bytes before the string data item's own declared end (0x00500452+10 = 0x0050045c). llm_tact_calc_dir24.asm 0x0042e156: FMUL double ptr [EDX+0x0050045a] (Ghidra's own generated comment reads 's__00500452+8', i.e. Ghidra itself derives the operand as an offset into the string, not as its own symbol).
findings.resolution: APPLIED, with the values independently re-derived rather than taken from the finding: read 24 bytes at 0x00500452 and unpacked them here -- 4d 49 4e 45 20 20 20 00 is 'MINE   ' plus terminator in 8 bytes, the next 8 unpack to exactly 180.0, and the 8 after that to M_PI (already named at 0x00500462), which is the giveaway: this is the 180.0 of the standard rad-to-deg conversion, and llm_tact_calc_dir24 computes llm_math_atan(dy/dx) * 180.0 / M_PI at 0x0042e153-0x0042e15c. Applied in TWO passes, because defining the double first CLEARS the overlapping string: pass 1 typed 0x0050045a as double, pass 2 re-applied TerminatedCString at 0x00500452, and I verified the end state (string len 8, double len 8, value 180). WIDER than the finding asked in one respect: also NAMED the double _G_LLM_MATH_HALF_TURN_DEG and plated both items, because the finding's actual complaint was that Ghidra rendered the operand as 's__00500452+8' -- shortening the string alone would have left it an unnamed DAT_. A whole-image instruction sweep confirms one referrer each (0x0042e156 for the double, 0x0042de70 MOV ESI,0x500452 for the string). EN v359.

findings.current: Named _G_LLM_KEY_LALT_HELD, i.e. a boolean saying the LEFT ALT key is down.
findings.proposed: The name asserts one specific key AND a boolean, and the access pattern supports neither -- it is a modifier-state BITMASK whose consumers all ask 'is either of bits 0/1 set'. A name of the _G_LLM_KEY_<MODIFIER>_STATE shape (bit 0 / bit 1 = left / right) is what the evidence supports. NOT renamed here because nothing settles WHICH modifier: the missing step is identifying the indexed key-state store that writes it.
findings.evidence: Typed byte 2026-08-27 (was `undefined`; tools/probe_global_widths.py reports SPLIT over the 72-byte extent, but all 13 probed sites are width 1 and 12 of them are at offset 0, so the BASE's width is settled). Every one of those 12 sites is a PAIR of mask tests and never a plain nonzero test: TEST byte ptr [0x00e69d48],0x1 immediately followed by TEST byte ptr [...],0x2 -- llm_tact_frame 0x00429f3a/0x00429f43 and 0x0042a034/0x0042a03d, llm_strat_input_update 0x00442086/0x0044208f, llm_strat_group_issue_attack_order 0x00444a2e/0x00444a37, llm_strat_group_issue_move_order_deferred 0x00444f2b/0x00444f34, llm_unit_ctrl_group_recall 0x004454f9/0x00445502. A whole-image instruction sweep over 252238 instructions finds NO direct writer, so the byte is written through an indexed key-state store; that index is what would name the modifier. Sibling two bytes on at 0x00e69d4a is tested TEST byte,0x3 (both bits at once) by llm_input_key_dequeue_translate_ascii at 0x004cb9ac -- consistent with a short run of per-modifier state bytes rather than one flag.
findings.resolution: APPLIED, but NOT as the finding proposed -- the rename was declined and the mechanism was settled instead, which is the more useful half. The finding's blocker was 'nothing settles WHICH modifier: a whole-image sweep finds NO direct writer'. The writers are indexed, so a sweep for the byte's own address CANNOT find them, and reading them settles everything. `0x00e69d48` is `_G_LLM_INPUT_KEYSTATE[0x38]` (base 0x00e69d10, 128 bytes), scan-code set 1 offset 0x38 = LEFT ALT. BIT LAYOUT, re-derived by me at every address a Sonnet read-only agent cited (I re-read all 23 instructions rather than trusting the report): bit 0 = the plain scancode is down; bit 1 = the E0-EXTENDED twin of the same scancode is down; bits 2/3 are set alongside 0/1 on key-down and never cleared on key-up (a sticky 'was pressed' pair with NO reader found -- still unconfirmed, and said so in the plate rather than guessed). Writers: llm_input_wndproc_tap 0x004d1194, index (lParam>>16)&0x7f at 0x004d156a/0x004d1614, extended = lParam bit 24 (TEST EBX,0x1000000 at 0x004d156d/0x004d1617), OR 0x5 at 0x004d157e (plain) vs OR 0xa at 0x004d1575 (extended), AND 0xfe at 0x004d1628 vs AND 0xfd at 0x004d161f; and llm_input_di_keyboard_poll 0x004d0a48, index dwOfs&0x7f at 0x004d0ab4, extended = the DIK top bit (DIK_RALT 0xb8), OR 0x5/0xa at 0x004d0ac9/0x004d0ac0, AND 0xfe/0xfd at 0x004d0ae0/0x004d0ad7. So bit 1 of THIS byte is RIGHT ALT, and the paired TEST 0x1 / TEST 0x2 at every consumer means 'either Alt' -- the finding's structural reading (bit0/bit1 = left/right) was RIGHT, for this byte. WHY THE RENAME WAS DECLINED, which is a judgement I am recording rather than burying: the finding asked for a family-uniform `_G_LLM_KEY_<MODIFIER>_STATE`. Bit 1 is LIVE only at LCTRL (0x1d) and LALT (0x38), because only Ctrl/Alt have E0 twins; at LSHIFT (0x2a), RSHIFT (0x36) and CAPSLOCK (0x3a) it is structurally dead -- those keys have their own plain scancodes. A left/right-encoding name would therefore be correct for two members and WRONG for three, and the five are named as a set. `_HELD` correctly describes bit 0, which is each byte's scancode identity and the bit every consumer treats as 'is this key down'. Kept all five names; put the full bit layout, the writers, the per-byte live/dead status of bit 1 and the unconfirmed bits 2/3 into a plate on EACH of the five (EN v363), superseding the plate that said the modifier was unknowable. WIDENED to the family, per the standing family rule: typed 0x00e69d2d/0x00e69d3a/0x00e69d46 `byte` (they were `undefined`; 0x00e69d48 was already byte), and NAMED the fifth member 0x00e69d4a -> `_G_LLM_KEY_CAPSLOCK_HELD` (was DAT_00e69d4a), on two independent legs: 0x00e69d4a - 0x00e69d10 = 0x3a = set-1 Caps Lock, and its sole reference 0x004cb9ac sits in the ToAscii shift-state gate right after the two Shift bytes. Also folded into docs/game-modes.md, whose 'bit 1 purpose unconfirmed -- possibly an edge/repeat companion bit' hedge was the stale half. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: _G_LLM_INPUT_KEYSTATE (0x00e69d10) is still typed `undefined`; a byte[128] there would swallow the five interior symbols, which are the useful handles. Recorded in its plate as accepted rather than left to look like an oversight.

findings.proposed: No DB change proposed (deleting/merging labels needs the user's explicit approval per CLAUDE.md, and the labels are harmless as documentation of the disp32 Ghidra chose) -- but the SEMANTIC finding is real and is now captured in tact_state.h's tile_vis_map_at() comment and in llm_tact_sidebar_dispatch/llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw's translation hazards instead: all three addresses are 4/5/6 bytes BEFORE the real _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP array (0x00713d20), and every observed write through them (llm_tact_sidebar_dispatch @0x00435a53/61/6f, llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw @0x00434662/7b) uses a COMPUTED index (VIEW_TILES_W-scaled) that, for every value actually reached (VIEW_TILES_W >= 1), lands INSIDE the real 300-byte _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP array, not in the 3-6 bytes the labels sit on. The three labels exist only because Ghidra's disp32 constant-folding picked the nearest preceding label (M6, 6 bytes before the array) as the base for `M6_addr + computed_offset` instead of `TILE_VIS_MAP_addr + (computed_offset - 6)`.
findings.evidence: docs/symbols.md: 0x00713d1a M6 (byte), 0x00713d1b M5 (byte), 0x00713d1c M4 (byte), 0x00713d20 _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP (byte[300]) -- M6 is exactly base-6, M5 base-5, M4 base-4. llm_tact_view_shift_col_inc (0x0043c0e1, this session's slice) ALSO writes through M6/M5/M4 at index 0 exactly (no offset), which is the one case that genuinely lands on the label bytes themselves rather than inside the array -- consistent with both being the same physical buffer, extended 6 bytes earlier than Ghidra's array type declares.
findings.resolution: MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND BROADER THAN REPORTED; THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM REJECTED; the widening question it left open is now ANSWERED NO. Applied at EN v370 as six EOL comments, no type change. BROADER: the finding said 'three separate 1-byte Ghidra labels'. There are SIX -- M6..M1 at 0x00713d1a..0x00713d1f, i.e. base-6 through base-1 of _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP (0x00713d20) -- with 9, 10, 8, 4, 4 and 4 referrers respectively, and every referrer of all six is from the same tactical UI drawing family (llm_tact_sidebar_dispatch, llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_draw/_multi_mode_tick, llm_tact_ui_draw_player_row_list, llm_tact_ui_sidebar_row_draw_left/_right, llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw/_ammo_draw, llm_tact_ui_order_buttons_minimap_tick, llm_tact_unit_draw_hp_bar_slot). Six consecutive one-byte 'globals' sharing one referrer family is the disp32-folding signature the finding described, at k = 1..6 rather than 4..6. The finding saw three because three were what its slice touched. REJECTED: 'llm_tact_view_shift_col_inc ALSO writes through M6/M5/M4 at index 0 exactly ... the one case that genuinely lands on the label bytes themselves'. It does not. That function (0x0043c0e1-0x0043c154, 39 instructions) makes exactly THREE outgoing data references -- _G_LLM_FRAMEBUFFER, _G_LLM_TACT_LOS_CACHE_PTR and _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP_PTR (0x00824ff4) -- and none to any of the six labels or to the array itself, and it appears in none of their referrer sets. It works through the runtime POINTER; the 'index 0' reading was a pointer access misread as a folded one. Note this was the finding's only UNCITED mechanical claim in the sense that mattered -- it named the function but not the instruction -- which is the tell the drain rule points at. THEREFORE WIDENING _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP TO byte[306] AT 0x00713d1a IS REJECTED, which is the judgement note_for_drain left open. With the index-0 write gone there is no evidence the buffer physically extends six bytes earlier; widening would bake the folding artifact into the type and move three registered state regions for it. The labels stay -- they are accurate documentation of the base Ghidra chose -- and each now carries the derivation as an EOL comment so the next reader does not re-open it. No C++ change: tact_state.h's tile_vis_map_at(index - 6) computes the same effective address either way, and the semantic note the finding put in the two translation hazards remains correct.
findings.note_for_drain: A judgement call, not a re-derivation: whether to WIDEN _G_LLM_TILE_VIS_MAP's Ghidra type to byte[306] starting at 0x00713d1a (absorbing the three labels) is a data-type change with unknown blast radius on other consumers of the current byte[300]-at-0x713d20 declaration, and is left open rather than guessed. This session worked around it in C++ by using tile_vis_map_at(index - 6) for the M6-relative writes rather than declaring a second region.

findings.current: map_object_unit.ai_group_index's field comment says only: 'Which AI tactical group (player_data.ai_groups[]) this unit belongs to; 0xffff = none. A third group concept, distinct from ctrl_group_id and move_group_id.' It describes the field as an INDEX with a sentinel and names no other writer.
findings.proposed: Extend the field comment (or split the field) to record that TWO functions treat the same 16-bit word as a BITFIELD, not an index: llm_unit_status_bit_set does `OR word ptr [EDX + 0xdd8d20],AX` @0x0044b0dd and llm_unit_status_bit_clear does `AND word ptr [EDX + 0xdd8d20],AX` @0x0044b132. An OR/AND of a mask into a slot documented as an index-with-0xffff-sentinel is either a second, undocumented use of those bits or a genuine aliasing bug, and the comment currently gives a reader no way to tell. Until it is settled, a reimplementation that treats the field purely as an index is reasoning from an incomplete plate.
findings.evidence: Image-wide instruction scan of all 252238 instructions of /eng/mh.exe for the little-endian dword 0x00dd8d20 (units base 0x00dd8c48 + 0xd8), 2026-08-28 -- independent of Ghidra's reference manager, which is docs/dead-ends.md's founding false negative. 22 sites. The AI writers ASSIGN a group index: llm_strat_ai_group_member_link @0x004d4a4e (MOV ..,SI), llm_strat_ai_group_remove @0x004d4f98 (MOV ..,DX), llm_strat_ai_group_member_unlink @0x004d49fc (MOV ..,0xffff), llm_strat_ai_notify_unit_lifecycle @0x004dbbae (MOV ..,0) / @0x004dbbce / @0x004dbd5b (MOV ..,0xffff). Four sim teardown writers CLEAR it: llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map @0x004874d8, llm_strat_unit_teardown_mapped @0x004876d3, llm_strat_unit_on_destroyed @0x004879b8, llm_strat_unit_teardown @0x00487d61, all `MOV word ptr [..],0x0`. The two above are the only READ-MODIFY-WRITE sites and the only ones whose operand is a variable mask in AX.
findings.resolution: APPLIED at EN v368, and WIDER than proposed -- the finding's mechanism is confirmed but its framing was wrong, and the correction changes what a reimplementation must do. Re-derived from raw disassembly: both functions build EDX from the same `player*0x5b04 + unit*0xe9` roster math map_object_unit itself uses, so 0xdd8d20 really is unit +0xd8 and this is NOT the disp32-folding artifact that produced finding 2026-08-27-2258-2 -- llm_unit_status_bit_set @0x0044b0dd `OR word ptr [EDX+0xdd8d20],AX` with AX = 1<<(bit_index&0x1f) built @0x0044b0c0-0x0044b0c5, and llm_unit_status_bit_clear @0x0044b132 `AND word ptr [EDX+0xdd8d20],AX` with AX complemented by `XOR dword ptr [local],0xffff` @0x0044b118. Neither touches any other field; a bit_index >= 16 is silently inert (only AX is written). WHAT THE FINDING GOT WRONG: it framed this as 'a second, undocumented use of those bits', i.e. an AI-side question. The CALL SITES say otherwise, which is exactly why they are the instrument and why an uncited meaning-claim is the suspect one. Each function has one static caller, both inside llm_strat_order_queue_dispatch's recovered switch, on order codes 0x34 ORDER_SYS_UNIT_STATUS_BIT_SET and 0x35 ORDER_SYS_UNIT_STATUS_BIT_CLEAR; those two codes are enqueued only by llm_strat_order_ctrlgrp_select_member @0x0046f1de and llm_strat_order_ctrlgrp_flash_member @0x0046f278, driven by llm_strat_unit_ctrlgroup_add_member/_remove_member/_leave, llm_unit_ctrl_group_activate/_flash_observer, llm_strat_selection_drag_finish and llm_ui_hud_unassigned_unit_row_click_handler. So the bits are the PLAYER'S Ctrl+digit CONTROL-GROUP feature and bit_index is the control-group number 0..9 -- literally the same value written to the sibling byte field ctrl_group_id (+0x2f) by llm_strat_unit_ctrlgroup_add_member. The `_raw` enqueue variants @0x0046f22b/@0x0046f2c5 have zero callers and are not the live path. AND THEREFORE THERE IS NO BIT SPLIT TO DOCUMENT, which is the finding's other proposal. AI group indices are 0..0x1f (bits 0-4) and the ctrl-group range 0..9 covers all of them, so every possible index value collides. A sweep of all 25 other accesses of the word -- 17 through the named field, 8 through the raw 0xdd8d20 + player*0x5b04 + unit*0xe9 form -- found every one treating it as a plain scalar (equality compare, array index, straight assignment) and NONE reading the bits back as flags. The two writers are write-only into an integer field: a genuine aliasing collision in the shipped binary, not a dual-purpose layout. Practically inert today because every AI writer returns early on !player_data[p].ai_enabled while the ctrl-group path always targets PlayerSide; the one path that could make it reachable is ORDER_SYS_PLAYER_SET_AI_HUMAN (0xf5) handing a slot between AI and human while a unit still holds a live index -- NOT traced, and left as the open item inside the field comment rather than as a separate queue entry. APPLIED: (1) map_object_unit.ai_group_index's field comment replaced -- writers, readers, sentinel, instruction addresses and the hazard, which is what the finding asked for; (2) SPLITTING THE FIELD IS REJECTED with reason -- the original does a raw unmasked OR/AND across the whole 16-bit word, so an index-bits/flag-bits split would misrepresent it, and mh_structs.gen.h's per-offset static_asserts plus M6 byte-parity need the authentic (buggy) shape; the field stays a plain ushort; (3) BEYOND THE FINDING, both llm_unit_status_bit_set/_clear plates were rewritten. They were wrong in their own right and would have kept misleading readers: the set plate said the target is `map::units[].f3` and that 'bit index arrives via an unresolved register artifact ... exact bit semantics unverified' (it is args[0] of the queued order, from the sole caller), and the clear plate suspected the FIELD NAME was a misnomer when the name is correct for all 20 assigning writers and every reader -- what is wrong is that a UI feature writes bits into the same word.

findings.evidence: map_FillDefaults zeroes it with `MOV EBX,0x3a980` / `XOR EDX,EDX` / `MOV EAX,0xcc46e0` / `CALL utils_fill_data` at 0x00456105-0x00456111. 0x3a980 = 240000. tools/data/state_regions.json independently records base 0xcc46e0 with size 240000 (name null, owner unknown), so the extent has two sources. Adjacent region _G_LLM_MAP_OBJECTS @0x00c86660 is `llm_map_object[10000]` and also 240000 bytes, i.e. 24 bytes per element -- suggestive of the same element type, but NOT evidence, and this finding does not claim it.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-31 (SIM-RESID-IF reopen, EN v381). 0x00cc46e0 typed `undefined1[240000]` -- extent only, element type deliberately not asserted -- and given a plate recording both extent sources (map_FillDefaults' 0x3a980 fill length and the save block table). The region now carries a name+extent in tools/data/state_regions.json and a sim_store base accessor (map_object_table_base()), which is what map_FillDefaults' fill needed.

findings.current: void __watcall llm_strat_invasion_due_check(void)
findings.proposed: int __watcall llm_strat_invasion_due_check(void)
findings.evidence: FIRST DERIVATION, from the body (tmp/decomp_sim_resid/llm_strat_invasion_due_check_0049949d.asm): both terminating paths materialise an explicit 0/1 flag into a local and load it into EAX immediately before the epilogue -- 0x0049951d `MOV dword ptr [EBP+-0x18],0x1` (the invasion-fired arm) and 0x00499526 `MOV dword ptr [EBP+-0x18],0x0` (the not-due arm) both fall into LAB_0049952d @0x0049952d `MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP+-0x18]`, then `LEA ESP,[EBP+-0x14]` / pops / `RET` @0x00499539. Every RET-reaching path is covered, so EAX is set deliberately on both. This is NOT the Watcom fake-return trap of docs/dead-ends.md:83 -- that trap is an UNCOMMITTED convention producing a CONCAT44 of leftover registers; here the convention is already committed __watcall and the value is a compiler-materialised 0/1 local. The identical shape one function away is already typed `int`: llm_strat_bldg_gather_nearby_squad_status @0x0044d468 ends 0x0044d80c `MOV EAX,[EBP-0x34]` / 0x0044d80f `MOV [EBP-0x10],EAX` / 0x0044d812 `MOV EAX,[EBP-0x10]` / RET and carries `int __mh_watcall_ebx_volatile`. SECOND DERIVATION, from the CALL SITES (ReVa find-cross-references, includeContext, this session): exactly TWO callers and BOTH DISCARD the value -- llm_strat_advance_sim_clock @0x0044d0ed calls it at 0x0044d14c on a bare statement line, and llm_strat_planet_transition_finalize @0x0044d160 calls it at 0x0044d187 likewise. That is why the wrong return type was invisible, and it is also why correcting it is behaviour-neutral for every existing caller.
findings.resolution: APPLIED 2026-08-31 (EN v382 -> v383) via tools/commit_prototypes.py OVERRIDE mode ({conv: __watcall}, ret int, no params -- AUTO mode cannot fire on a zero-parameter function, which is exactly why this one was never auto-corrected). NOTHING DIFFERS from the first reading: the body derivation and the call-site derivation agree, the second only adding WHY it went unnoticed. Ripple accepted rather than deferred: mh_calls.gen.h's callable becomes int32_t, so src/mh_dll/libmh/lockstep/turn_engine.{h,cpp}'s `void (*invasion_due_check)()` member and its live binding were retyped int32_t (value still discarded, as the original callers discard it). The translation in src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/resid/sim_invasion_due_check.cpp returns the flag.
